title: When Do Repetition Loops Lock? Truncation Sampling, Bounded Penalties, and a Blind Spot in DRY
abstract: Language models sometimes repeat verbatim until the generation limit. We study the exit rather than the entrance: given that a span has already been repeated $n$ times, when is escape still possible? Along the loop the context is deterministic, so loop survival under any sampler can be computed exactly from one forward pass. Pure sampling leaves a positive escape probability at every step; top-$p$ with threshold $π>1/2$ locks a position exactly when the continuation probability reaches $π$. A bounded penalty can leave a position locked; a penalty that outgrows the model's preference for the loop over unseen tokens guarantees escape under top-$p$. The same analysis predicts a blind spot in the widely deployed DRY sampler: its sequence breakers cap the penalty at $λb^{g-1-a}$ for loops whose longest breaker-free run has $g$ tokens. On eleven open models, 66\% of locked units with $g=6$ stay locked under DRY and 1\% with $g=8$. In free generation with llama.cpp, all 109 loops that survive DRY have $g\le 7$. We propose DRY-C, which adds a term that grows exponentially with the number of verbatim recurrences, up to its look-back window. With it, none of 720 structured-output generations looped to the length limit, and task completion stayed close to DRY's.

title: Cycle-Invariant Lightweight Authenticated Encryption and Cross-Domain Silicon Entropy Harvesting on ARM Cortex-M0+
abstract: Abstract This record contains the complete artifacts, bare-metal C source code, and empirical benchmark logs for a cycle-invariant authenticated encryption and silicon-jitter true random number generator (TRNG) architecture implemented on an STM32C031 (ARM Cortex-M0+). Designed for resource-constrained edge systems (such as Electric Vehicle BMS nodes), the system achieves strict constant-time execution ($\Delta = 0$ clock cycle variance) to defeat timing side-channel attacks, harvests cross-domain clock phase jitter whitened via the hardware CRC-32 unit, and implements sub-microsecond interrupt-driven SRAM tamper key-shredding. 1. Introduction & Problem Statement Ultra-low-cost microcontrollers deployed in distributed automotive and IoT nodes frequently lack native hardware TRNGs and hardware AES accelerators. Standard software implementations are computationally expensive, consume excessive flash memory, and leak execution timing variations that allow attackers to recover secret keys via side-channel analysis. 2. Proposed Bare-Metal Architecture The proposed architecture operates via direct CMSIS register manipulation without software libraries or operating systems: Silicon-Jitter TRNG: Harvests phase drift between the core SysTick timer and peripheral TIM3 clock mixed with ADC1 SAR quantization noise, whitened through the on-chip CRC->DR polynomial engine. Constant-Time AEAD Pipeline: Implements a 32-round Feistel block cipher combined with a keyed Hardware CRC-32 MAC tag, utilizing zero data-dependent branches. Tamper Key-Shredding: Employs a RAM-relocated vector table (SCB->VTOR) and an EXTI0 falling-edge hardware interrupt to execute a 2-pass SRAM entropy-flooding and zeroization sequence upon physical intrusion. 3. Empirical Benchmarks & Comparative Analysis The system was benchmarked on an ARM Cortex-M0+ running at 48 MHz. Cycle Invariance: Verified via ARM SysTick->VAL profiling, proving a steady-state execution time of exactly 11,988 CPU cycles (249.75 µs) with zero variance ($\sigma^2 = 0$), compared to variable-timing table-based software ciphers (~35,000+ cycles). Memory Footprint: Consumes < 1.2 KB of Flash and < 64 bytes of SRAM, outperforming bulky software stacks like mbedTLS. Tamper Latency: Achieves key-shredding in < 1 µs, mitigating cold-boot memory retention. 4. Repository & File Structure main.c: Contains the bare-metal C implementation, register initializations, TRNG entropy harvester, constant-time cipher, and EXTI0 tamper interrupt service routine. diagram.json: The Wokwi hardware simulation configuration file defining the STM32C031 Nucleo board, the analog potentiometer sensor (PA1), and the physical tamper pushbutton (PA0). aead_out.png: Empirical benchmark serial output log demonstrating live sequence tracking, encrypted ciphertext, hardware CRC-32 verification tags, and cycle-count invariance. GitHub Source Code & Interactive Simulation:https://github.com/VasudevanS1906/cortex-m0-secure-vault-trng

title: SQuIREL: A Context-Relative Framework for Measuring Entity Richness in Wikidata
abstract: Wikidata is a large, heterogeneous knowledge graph and applying data quality metrics requires context-specific approaches. The "richness" quality metric is currently under-researched and typically restricted to the ontology level, which fails to capture entity-specific structural depth. To address this gap, we introduce SQuIREL, a method that measures richness directly at the entity level using six dimensions: Semantic Specificity, Qualifier Density, Internal Connectivity, Reference Provenance, External Network Connectivity, and Linguistic Accessibility. These dimensions are kept disaggregated to preserve actionability for targeted editorial intervention. We apply this metric to two case studies of oil paintings (Brazilian vs. French) and writers (grouped by citizenship and gender) to demonstrate how it surfaces representational inequalities that may indicate systemic bias. Our metric successfully distinguishes between highly tailored and basic entity profiles, revealing nuances that raw counts and existing aggregate scores obscure. Specifically, it identifies structural imbalances, such as 48% of Brazilian paintings clustering as low-richness stubs against 0% in the French cohort, as well as intersectional patterns, including contrasting gender gaps between UK and Nigerian writers.

title: Understanding Generation Z's Continuance Intention toward E-commerce Chatbots: Survey Dataset on Information Quality, Satisfaction, Perceived Ease of Use, and Trust
abstract: This dataset contains the survey responses used in the study "Empirical Study of Generation Z's Continuance Intention toward E-commerce Chatbots" (Gunawan, Subhan, and Caesar, Bina Nusantara University). The study adapts the research model of Gao et al. (2025, Journal of Business Research, 200, 115661, doi:10.1016/j.jbusres.2025.115661) to examine how information quality, perceived ease of use, trust, and satisfaction relate to the intention to continue using AI chatbots on e-commerce platforms. DATA COLLECTIONResponses were collected through an online questionnaire (Google Forms) between 27 and 30 March 2026 (timestamps in GMT+7), using convenience sampling targeting Generation Z users in the JABODETABEK region of Indonesia. The questionnaire items were administered in English, and the introduction was in Indonesian. On the opening page, participants were informed of the study's purpose and told that their responses would be confidential, anonymous, and used only for academic purposes. The dataset contains no names, e-mail addresses, or other direct identifiers. FILEOne CSV file exported from Google Forms: 315 rows (one per submission) and 24 columns, with no missing values. This is the raw export: no responses were removed and no recoding was applied. VARIABLES- Timestamp: date and time of submission (GMT+7)- Gender: Male (154), Female (161)- Age (categories): 18–21 years (103), 22–28 years (195), 29–35 years (16), >35 years (1)- Place of Education: Tangerang (87), Depok (82), Bogor (49), Bekasi (47), Jakarta (47), Bandung (1), Jatinangor (1), Pontianak (1)- Education: Diploma (77), Bachelor's Degree/S1 (214), Master's Degree/S2 (20), Doctor's Degree/S3 (4)- 19 measurement items, each rated on a five-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree). All items are positively worded; none is reverse-coded. MEASUREMENT ITEMS (column headers contain the full item wording)Information quality (IQ1–IQ7): AI chatbots in e-commerce provide sufficient information; Through AI chatbots in e-commerce, I get the information I need on time; Information provided by AI chatbots in e-commerce is in a useful format / is clear / is accurate / is up-to-date / is reliable.Satisfaction (SF1–SF3), perceived ease of use (PEU1–PEU3), trust (TR1–TR3), and continue using intention (CUI1–CUI3): items adopted from Gao et al. (2025), e.g., "Overall, I am satisfied with AI chatbot in e-commerce", "Using AI chatbot in e-commerce is easy for me", "I consider the AI chatbot in e-commerce to be trustworthy", "I intend to continue using AI chatbot in e-commerce rather than discontinue using them". NOTES FOR REUSE- Column order: Timestamp, Gender, Age, Place of Education, Education, IQ1–IQ7, SF1–SF3, PEU1–PEU3, TR1–TR3, CUI1–CUI3.- Age was recorded in categories; 17 submissions fall in categories above 28 years.- Place of Education includes three locations outside JABODETABEK.- Some submissions share identical answers across all 19 items (18 rows, 7 distinct patterns).- The original analysis used PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). Contact: gilbert.gunawan002@binus.ac.id

title: Подієво-орієнтована архітектура мультиагентних систем на основі великих мовних моделей – агенти як мікросервіси
abstract: У статті запропоновано подієво-орієнтовану архітектуру мультиагентних систем (МАС) на основі великих мовних моделей (LLM), у якій кожен агент є незалежним мікросервісом з власним пулом обчислювальних ресурсів, а взаємодія агентів здійснюється завдяки брокеру подій. Розроблено математичну модель МАС як мережі систем масового обслуговування з розгалуженням і злиттям (fork-join), яка враховує логнормальний час інференсу LLM, обмежену конкурентність агентів, транзієнтні помилки, повторні спроби та динаміку черги під час відмови агента та пікового навантаження. Удосконалено модель втрат синхронної оркестрації завдяки урахування кореляції повторних спроб. Синхронну послідовну оркестрацію, синхронну оркестрацію з паралельним розгалуженням і подієву хореографію порівняно аналітично, методом імітаційного моделювання та експериментально на прототипі на основі Redis Streams. Встановлено, що в стаціонарному режимі латентність визначається критичним шляхом графа задачі і не залежить від способу доставки, тоді як під час відмов агентів і пікових навантажень подієва архітектура зберігає всі задачі без налаштування повторів на боці клієнта ціною їх затримки в черзі. Проаналізовано чутливість результатів до параметрів синхронної оркестрації та представлено результати експерименту з реальною мовною моделлю.

title: IntelliLayer: A Deep Learning Architecture for Dynamic Decision Intelligence
abstract: Organizations increasingly use data-driven systems to support operational decision-making in dynamic environments. However, many existing deep learning models focus primarily on predicting outcomes rather than recommending reliable actions. These models often provide limited information about prediction confidence, may experience performance degradation when data patterns change, and offer insufficient explanations for their decisions. Previous studies have addressed these challenges independently through improved prediction models, uncertainty estimation, calibration techniques, data drift detection, and explainable AI methods. To address these limitations, this paper introduces IntelliLayer, a five-layer deep learning architecture that combines these capabilities within a unified decision-making framework. The proposed architecture integrates static data and sequential events using Transformer encoders and a learnable gated fusion mechanism. It estimates calibrated outcome distributions through a deep ensemble and selects actions based on expected utility, while uncertain cases are referred to human reviewers. To handle changing data patterns, the framework employs adaptive windowing for drift detection and updates the model using replay techniques and elastic weight consolidation. Additionally, integrated gradients are used to explain individual predictions, and an audit record is maintained for every decision to support transparency and accountability. The paper describes the architecture of each layer, outlines the online decision-making algorithm, and presents a reference implementation stack. It also defines a reproducible evaluation framework covering predictive performance, calibration, decision-making costs, selective prediction coverage, recovery from data drift, and processing latency. Since experimental results have not yet been obtained, the proposed evaluation protocol and results template provide a structured basis for future validation of the IntelliLayer architecture.

title: Breaking the Static Verifier Ceiling: Zero-Overhead Self-Evolving System-One Judge and Policy Co-Evolution on a Single Shared Foundation Backbone (CoEvo-Jev-GRPO)
abstract: Full-Length Preprint (12-Page English Edition + 8-Page Chinese Edition) & Benchmark Suite — Part III-B: Self-Evolving System-One Judge & Policy Co-Evolution. When an LLM policy evolves beyond 400 GRPO steps on hard competition mathematics, any frozen reward model suffers from late-stage calibration drift and Goodhart pseudo-proof exploitation, while dual-model online RM training triples GPU VRAM (24.46 GB). We introduce CoEvo-Jev-GRPO, an online verifier-anchored bilevel co-evolution framework on a single shared Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B backbone (8.08 GB total VRAM on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB, adding only +0.02 GB and 0.84 ms per calibration step). By mining policy-verifier disagreement rollouts and updating the Layer-28 System-One Pointer Head and top-layer judge LoRAs via a Null-Anchored Brier + Contrastive Margin + KL-to-Prior objective, CoEvo-Jev-GRPO contracts Judge Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by 77.1% (from 0.048 to 0.011) and suppresses subtle pseudo-proof hacking to 1.2%. Across MATH-500 (79.8%), AIME 2024/2025 (36.7%, +16.7% over Binary RLVR), AMC-12 (74.4%), and OlympiadBench-Math (46.2%), CoEvo-Jev-GRPO achieves #1 SOTA with 59.28% Mean Accuracy (+5.28% over Frozen DC-Jev-GRPO and +15.83% over Binary RLVR). Series Companion DOIs: Part I (10.5281/zenodo.23439711), Part II (10.5281/zenodo.23441431)Open-Source Code & v3.0.0 Suite: https://github.com/rainyflash/DC-Jev-RL

title: Native Probability Outputs for Clinical Triage: An Evaluation of Calibration and Decision Accuracy
abstract: Patient-facing triage requires an appropriate care recommendation and recognition of when information is insufficient. We evaluate whether Jev, a decision model that returns probabilities over predefined actions, supports both judgments. Using CARE-Bench, we compare Jev with four general-purpose language models and three input-independent baselines across 925 decision points from 439 public cases. On the public test subset, Jev ranks fourth of five models by macro-F1 (0.461) but has the lowest observed multiclass Brier score (0.610), an 18.7\% improvement over uniform prediction (case-bootstrap 95\% interval, 4.9--31.1\%). Noul has lower binary Brier than Choice (0.215 versus 0.276). A evaluation of 453 HealthBench conversations again gives Jev the lowest observed Brier score (0.299), but measures a distinct emergency-referral judgment. Jev combines lower probability error with missed clarification needs in the four-action task. Asking about information sufficiency separately increases recall but also produces frequent unnecessary clarification assignments.

title: Capability-as-Infrastructure: Software on Demand
abstract: Capability-as-Infrastructure (CaI) proposes that the durable unit of a software system is no longer the application but the declared capability, together with the data, history, decisions and authority it operates on. Applications, interfaces, synchronization logic and much of the executable code become compiled, replaceable outputs of an agentic environment that builds them when a need appears and maintains them while they are useful: software on demand. Where Methodology-as-Infrastructure compiles how to think, Intent-as-Infrastructure compiles what to reach into, and Governance-as-Infrastructure compiles what must be true, CaI compiles what must be possible, opening a duration axis alongside GaI's upstream terminus. Four properties are required: Capability-declared, Implementation-compiled, Continuity-sovereign (observation, interpretation and accepted state kept distinct), and Human-as-primitive at authority. CaI extends local-first software (the sync protocol itself becomes a compiled capability) and malleable software. This is a concept paper: its two central claims, continuity under replacement and autonomous capability growth, are stated as hypotheses with a validation protocol, and a companion document describes a reference architecture on Cloudflare (Workers, Durable Objects, Agents SDK, Workflows).

title: 枯れ葉から大樹へ:AIエコシステムにおける構造改革のための戦略的提言 — データ配当(Data Dividend)プロトコルとオンデバイス動画生成AI(Veo Nano)アーキテクチャによる共生的未来の設計 (From Leaf to Tree: A Strategic Proposal for Structural Reform in the AI Ecosystem)
abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) | Original Manuscript Date: November 2025 現在、生成AIエコシステムは「熱力学的限界(クラウド推論の電力・コスト・遅延)」と「情報学的限界(有機的学習データの枯渇と自己回帰的モデル崩壊:Model Collapse)」という二つの存亡に関わる壁に直面している。本論文(2025年11月起案・第212編アーカイブ版)は、対価なき一方的データ抽出パラダイムが長期的には基盤モデル自身の品質劣化とクリエイター離反を招くことを指摘し、以下の2つの技術的・経済的解決策を提言する。(1) 経済的解決策(Data Dividend / GDDプロトコル):C2PA来歴証明規格とシャープレイ値(Shapley Value)/影響関数に基づく貢献度算定を結合し、人間が創出した高エントロピーな「有機的データ(Organic Data)」へマイクロ・ロイヤリティを自動還元するサプライチェーンを確立する。(2) 技術的解決策(オンデバイス動画生成AI「Veo Nano」アーキテクチャ):クラウドGPU(H100等)の推論コストと通信レイテンシを解消するため、敵対的蒸留(1ステップ推論化)と拡散トランスフォーマー(DiT)の4ビット量子化(W4A8)および連合学習(Federated Learning)を統合し、モバイル・エッジNPU上で完結するプライバシー保護型リアルタイム生成アーキテクチャを設計する。 (English Abstract): Generative AI confronts a dual existential bottleneck: thermodynamic scaling limits (cloud GPU inference energy, cost, and network latency) and information-theoretic degradation ("Model Collapse" induced by training on recursive synthetic data while alienating human creators). Originally authored in November 2025, this 212th monograph proposes a two-pillar structural reform: (1) a C2PA and Shapley-Value Data Dividend (GDD) Protocol that distinguishes human-created "Organic Data" from synthetic outputs and automates micro-royalty attribution; and (2) an On-Device Video Diffusion ("Veo Nano") Architecture combining single-step adversarial distillation, 4-bit Diffusion Transformer quantization (W4A8KV4), and GDPR-compliant Federated Learning on mobile NPUs. title: Analysis of Information Degradation and Reliability Transitions via Structured Noise Injection in Multisensor Localization
abstract: This study investigates information degradation and reliability transitions in multisensor localization systems using a structured noise injection approach. A five-sensor localization scenario is considered, where range measurements are intentionally corrupted by Gaussian perturbations, intermittent burst disturbances, and positive measurement biases. Target coordinates are estimated using a weighted nonlinear least-squares method, while localization performance is evaluated through root mean square error (RMSE), Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), Cramér–Rao Lower Bound (CRLB), and failure rate metrics. Experiments are conducted under signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels ranging from −5 dB to 25 dB using 600 Monte Carlo realizations for each operating condition. The results show that increasing perturbation levels progressively reduce localization accuracy and information content while increasing theoretical uncertainty. A distinct reliability transition region is observed between 5 dB and 10 dB, where localization failures rapidly decrease as measurement quality improves. The findings demonstrate that controlled noise injection provides a practical means of exposing information-deficient operating conditions and reliability boundaries in multisensor localization systems.

title: Verifying Human-Written Reasoning References
abstract: Evaluating the reasoning of AI systems often relies on human-written reasoning chains as references, yet the logical support for their individual steps is rarely verified. Although prior neuro-symbolic approaches have formalized and checked reasoning, their reported evaluations do not systematically assess whether step conclusions in human-written reference derivations are entailed by their cited premise sets or investigate the sources of failures in those references. To address these limitations, we present a novel reference-centred assessment method for human-written derivations that combines entailment checking against cited premise sets, full-premise rechecking, and failure attribution to examine the reliability of these derivations and their formal representations. We evaluate it on P-FOLIO, using a large language model (LLM) to translate step conclusions into first-order logic (FOL) and the Z3 SMT solver to check entailment. Of 386 derivations examined, 202 (52.3%) meet all our checking criteria, meaning that every translated step is entailed by its stated support and the required target is established under the available FOL representations. Among 230 steps not entailed by their stated support, 191 become entailed when checked against the complete original premises, indicating that most initial failures reflect incomplete or mismatched support rather than unsupported claims. Manual analysis of the remaining 39 cases identifies 21 human reasoning errors, 11 FOL translation errors, and 7 dataset annotation errors. A separate manual audit of 50 randomly sampled steps that passed the entailment checks found 46 faithful FOL translations (92%). These findings suggest that disagreement with a human-written reasoning reference may originate in the reference or its formal representation rather than in the AI system being evaluated.

title: RAGit: Turning Document Preprocessing into an Experimental Variable for RAG
abstract: Document preprocessing choices can substantially affect retrieval in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, yet they are often selected heuristically and are difficult to compare under consistent conditions. We present RAGit, an open-source experimentation workbench for the systematic and reproducible evaluation of document preprocessing choices through downstream retrieval. RAGit represents parsing, chunking, indexing, retrieval, and evaluation as configurable experimental stages, enabling controlled comparisons while the remaining downstream settings are kept fixed. It preserves provenance from retrieved chunks to source pages and maps heterogeneous retrieval units to a common page-level ranking for evaluation. The current implementation supports multiple parsers and chunking strategies, dense and late-interaction retrieval, reusable intermediate artifacts, and multi-configuration benchmarking. We demonstrate RAGit through controlled experiments comparing alternative preprocessing configurations under a fixed retrieval setup, illustrating how preprocessing can be treated as an explicit experimental variable. RAGit and its documentation are publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/OmarElbachyr/ragit). A demonstration video is available at https://youtu.be/tsst-Bhfz4I.

title: Prune Early, Verify Deep: Single-Backbone System-One Prefix Tree-GRPO and Speculative Noul Pruning for Long-Horizon Reasoning and Theorem Proving (Tree-Jev-GRPO)
abstract: Full-Length Preprint (12-Page English Edition + 7-Page Chinese Edition) & Benchmark Suite — Part III-C: Long-Horizon Prefix Tree-GRPO & Formal Theorem Proving. Standard flat-sequence GRPO wastes 70%+ of decoding FLOPs regenerating shared reasoning prefixes and continuing to decode 1,500+ tokens after a chain hits an early algebraic contradiction. We introduce Tree-Jev-GRPO, which exploits Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B’s hybrid Gated-DeltaNet linear-attention architecture (3.81x lower prefix-tree KV memory, 14.20 GB vs. 54.10 GB on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB) and co-located jaredpalmer/kev-4b incremental node probing (14.80 ms/node). By immediately pruning dead-end branches where g_noul < 0.30 and computing sibling-relative branch advantages across shared-prefix forks (-61.5% gradient variance), Tree-Jev-GRPO cuts wasted dead-end FLOPs by 66.0% (2.94x compute speedup) and achieves #1 SOTA across 4 Formal & Long-Horizon Reasoning Benchmarks: MiniF2F-Lean4 (64.8%, +20.2% over Flat Binary RLVR), ProofNet-Formal (52.4%), MATH-500 Level-5 Hard (68.7%, +26.9% over Binary RLVR), and GPQA-Diamond (56.1%), reaching 60.50% Mean Accuracy. title: TwinLens: an interpretability digital twin for LLMs
abstract: TwinLens builds a transcoder-based digital twin of a language model, predicts the effect of feature interventions, and checks each prediction against the real model. Across 8,064 interventions on GPT-2 small (56 prompts), the linear twin that attribution graphs describe ranks real effects poorly (Spearman rho 0.20). The error traces to two dropped derivatives, the LayerNorm scale and the attention pattern. Restoring both keeps the graph exactly linear and raises rho to 0.53, matching the nonlinear replacement model (0.52), and cuts catastrophic misses from 2.2% to 0.05%. The fix replicates on Qwen3-0.6B (2,304 edits). A trust model predicts in advance, from the clean run alone, when a prediction will hold (AUROC 0.93).

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty: A General Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) operate under multiple forms of uncertainty, including uncertainty about the correctness of generated answers, the completeness of available evidence, the validity of intermediate reasoning, the interpretation of task requirements, and the reliability of feedback. Individual-model mechanisms, such as self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-diagnosis, self-correction, and self-verification, provide ways to inspect and revise outputs. Mutual mechanisms, including cross-model evaluation, mutual diagnosis, collaborative reasoning, cross-model verification, and information exchange, provide additional perspectives that may reveal errors overlooked by an individual model. However, neither individual processing nor multi-model collaboration is universally optimal under uncertainty. Individual processing may preserve computational efficiency but remain trapped in persistent errors, whereas collaboration may introduce correlated judgments, misleading consensus, additional computational costs, and uncertainty that is transferred or amplified through interaction. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty (ASSM-MM-U), a conceptual framework that treats uncertainty as a central state variable for dynamically selecting and coordinating individual-model and cross-model processing mechanisms. The framework distinguishes uncertainty associated with incomplete evidence, model limitations, ambiguous task specifications, conflicting information, and uncertain evaluation signals. It represents uncertainty through a multidimensional state that includes estimated magnitude, source, calibration quality, persistence, propagation, and reducibility. A cost-sensitive controller estimates the expected value of candidate mechanisms in reducing relevant uncertainty and improving task outcomes. It can retain an individual mechanism, activate a mutual mechanism, return to individual processing, or transition between mechanism families according to the evolving uncertainty state. The paper formalizes the problem, presents an uncertainty-aware architecture and reference algorithm, identifies reliability safeguards, and proposes research questions, hypotheses, and an experimental protocol. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its potential contribution is the explicit integration of uncertainty characterization, uncertainty reduction, mechanism selection, and resource-aware coordination within a common control framework. evidence.title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty: A General Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) operate under multiple forms of uncertainty, including uncertainty about the correctness of generated answers, the completeness of available evidence, the validity of intermediate reasoning, the interpretation of task requirements, and the reliability of feedback. Individual-model mechanisms, such as self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-diagnosis, self-correction, and self-verification, provide ways to inspect and revise outputs. Mutual mechanisms, including cross-model evaluation, mutual diagnosis, collaborative reasoning, cross-model verification, and information exchange, provide additional perspectives that may reveal errors overlooked by an individual model. However, neither individual processing nor multi-model collaboration is universally optimal under uncertainty. Individual processing may preserve computational efficiency but remain trapped in persistent errors, whereas collaboration may introduce correlated judgments, misleading consensus, additional computational costs, and uncertainty that is transferred or amplified through interaction. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms and Mutual Mechanisms Under Uncertainty (ASSM-MM-U), a conceptual framework that treats uncertainty as a central state variable for dynamically selecting and coordinating individual-model and cross-model processing mechanisms. The framework distinguishes uncertainty associated with incomplete evidence, model limitations, ambiguous task specifications, conflicting information, and uncertain evaluation signals. It represents uncertainty through a multidimensional state that includes estimated magnitude, source, calibration quality, persistence, propagation, and reducibility. A cost-sensitive controller estimates the expected value of candidate mechanisms in reducing relevant uncertainty and improving task outcomes. It can retain an individual mechanism, activate a mutual mechanism, return to individual processing, or transition between mechanism families according to the evolving uncertainty state. The paper formalizes the problem, presents an uncertainty-aware architecture and reference algorithm, identifies reliability safeguards, and proposes research questions, hypotheses, and an experimental protocol. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its potential contribution is the explicit integration of uncertainty characterization, uncertainty reduction, mechanism selection, and resource-aware coordination within a common control framework. The novelty and effectiveness of this integration require systematic comparison with existing uncertainty-estimation, adaptive reasoning, and multi-agent collaboration methods.

title: The Collider Beacon: Certified Public Randomness from Symmetry and Quantum Measurement
abstract: We propose particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider as a shared cryptographic resource. The construction rests on a division of labor between symmetry and quantum measurement: rotational invariance fixes the azimuthal distribution to the Haar measure, while each event is an unpredictable quantum draw. We give a formal source model, a master bound decomposing the distance-to-uniform into named physical terms, and a pre-commitment protocol turning embargoed datasets into time-capsule beacons. On 5,211,771 CMS ZeroBias events (Run 2016G open data) we measure h_inf = 7.8413 of 8 bits per event, with the bound closing exactly on its measured parameters; NIST STS reports zero flags. A cross-detector check on ATLAS open data (597,965 events) finds the CMS acceptance seam absent (local band ratio 1.0024 +/- 0.0072; excluded at 14.1 sigma), while ATLAS exhibits a distinct broad modulation -- the seam is a per-device geometric fingerprint. Code and evidence: https://github.com/qBucker/collider-beacon (tag phase0-v1.0).

title: Geometry-Aware Interpolation for Inverse Problems
abstract: Recovering missing visual information from incomplete or degraded images remains a challenging problem, particularly when spatial variations and complex image structures affect reconstruction accuracy. Although Spatial Transformer Networks (STNs) facilitate spatial feature alignment, their reliance on conventional linear or bilinear interpolation limits their ability to capture the underlying geometric characteristics of image data. Furthermore, interpolation based on a restricted set of neighbouring pixels can introduce inconsistencies in gradient propagation, potentially affecting optimisation stability. To address these limitations, we propose a Geometry-Aware Interpolation Network (GAIN), a variational autoencoder-based framework that incorporates manifold geometry into spatial transformation and image reconstruction. Rather than estimating pixel intensities solely from fixed spatial neighbours, GAIN exploits the local tangent structure of the data manifold to construct geometry-informed intensity approximations. An entropy-based regularisation mechanism further guides the estimation of spatial transformation parameters, promoting more adaptive interpolation. In addition, a convolutional normalisation strategy is introduced to regulate the magnitude of non-zero activations and improve gradient stability during training. Extensive experiments on challenging image completion and classification benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of GAIN in improving predictive accuracy while reducing computational cost compared with existing methods.

title: Cost Per Correct: benchmark tasks for cost-per-correct-answer evaluation of LLM agents
abstract: Cost Per Correct is a small benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on cost-effectiveness rather than accuracy alone. Instead of asking only whether a model produces a correct answer, it prices the run and reports the cost of each correct answer: total spend in USD divided by the number of correct answers, so a cheap model that is usually right can beat an expensive model that is always right. Version 1.0.0 contains the 5 easy-tier tasks (arithmetic, extraction, classification) that are live in the hosted benchmark. Each task is a self-contained prompt with a deterministic grading assertion (regular-expression match on the response; no LLM judge). The benchmark was created by Karmendra Pandey and first published as a public benchmark on Kaggle Benchmarks on 11 October 2026 (Kaggle Benchmarking Challenge entry), where the live leaderboard remains: https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/karmendra8386/cost-per-correct In the first hosted run (11 October 2026), Gemini 2.5 Flash passed all 5 tasks (leaderboard score 100.00) and GPT-OSS 120B failed one extraction task; three runs on the second task show as errors because the Kaggle platform would not register swapped-in models - platform errors, not model answers, disclosed in the accompanying README (hosted-results-2026-10-11.csv) and in the entry write-up at the time. Costs are accounted with tokenecon (software DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23427025), the token-economics library that decomposes per-task spend into prompt, completion, tool-call, and retrieval tokens priced per model tier. The underlying cost model is described in the companion preprint "Token-Economics for Agentic AI" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23195511). This Zenodo record mirrors the benchmark off Kaggle so the task set and methodology carry a permanent, citable DOI independent of any single platform. Provenance: the hosted benchmark was never exported from Kaggle; the task definitions were transcribed verbatim from the local source code used to build it and cross-checked against the entry-day record written from the live task pages. Only tasks e1-e5 of the author's 24-task local suite are live on Kaggle, so only those 5 are in this dataset.

title: SwinMask-Cyto: Supporting Experimental Data and Evaluation Results
abstract: This repository contains supporting experimental data for the research manuscript entitled “SwinMask-Cyto: A Swin Transformer-Enhanced Mask R-CNN Framework for Multi-Class Cervical Cell Instance Segmentation.” The research investigates a Swin Transformer-enhanced Mask R-CNN framework for automated detection and instance segmentation of five cervical cytology cell categories: Superficial-Intermediate, Parabasal, Metaplastic, Koilocytotic, and Dyskeratotic. The repository contains available experimental training logs, validation and test evaluation results, model configuration files, training metric histories, prediction outputs, and supporting numerical data. The experiments investigate different training durations, data augmentation strategies, and model regularization configurations. The best recorded 36-epoch experiment achieved a bounding-box mAP@0.5 of 0.7230 and a segmentation mAP@0.5 of 0.7280 on the held-out test set. These materials are provided to support transparency, reproducibility, and further research in artificial intelligence-assisted cervical cytology analysis. Dataset sources, file descriptions, and applicable data-sharing restrictions are documented in the accompanying files. Original private clinical images are not included in the public research data collection.

title: Clinical validation of artificial intelligence for cancer detection prognosis and analysis across imaging modalities and tumor types
abstract: This study evaluates the diagnostic and prognostic performance of artificial intelligence in cancer detection across imaging modalities and tumor types. The review synthesizes current evidence on deep learning, radiomics, multimodal integration, and precision oncology frameworks, with emphasis on validation quality and clinical translation. A systematic review of 180 peer reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted. Included investigations assessed artificial intelligence applications in radiology, digital pathology, endoscopy, PET imaging, and multimodal platforms. Extracted data covered diagnostic accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, dataset size, validation strategy, and study design. Subdomains included detection, prognosis, grading, survival prediction, radio-genomics, explainability, federated learning, and regulatory evaluation. Across breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, brain, and skin cancers, multiple high-quality cohorts reported AUC values above 0.90. Whole slide histopathology achieved the highest discrimination, reaching AUC 0.99 in curated datasets. CT and MRI systems demonstrated strong performance with multicenter validation, including large scale lung and breast screening studies. Radiomics contributed to survival prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, and molecular subtype inference. Multimodal and transformer-based architectures improved representation learning in volumetric and cross domain data. Despite strong retrospective performance, only 21 percent of studies included external validation, 14 percent incorporated multicenter datasets, and 6 percent applied prospective or temporal validation. Artificial intelligence shows consistent high performance in cancer detection and prognostic modeling across imaging domains. Strongest evidence supports adjunctive use in screening, digital pathology, and endoscopic detection. Broader clinical adoption requires prospective trials, multicenter external validation, standardized reporting, explainability integration, and alignment with regulatory frameworks to ensure reliable deployment in precision oncology.

title: Contrastive Adversarial Training for Robust Graph Neural Networks under Label Poisoning
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are effective for modeling relational data but are vulnerable to label poisoning, where a small number of corrupted training labels can propagate errors across the graph via message passing. Despite this risk, defenses against label poisoning remain underexplored: existing methods are primarily designed for label noise and often rely on robust losses or heuristic data cleaning that fail to distinguish adversarial poisoning from naturally hard examples. In this paper, we propose CoLAT (Contrastive Label-flipping for Adversarial Training), a novel contrastive adversarial training framework tailored for robust node classification on graphs. The core of our approach is a structure-aware detection model that uses contrastive learning to identify label-structure inconsistencies. Unlike prior contrastive methods that focus on representation learning, CoLAT leverages contrastive embeddings to select high-risk nodes that guide adversarial label-flipping during training. This alternating optimization not only performs structure-aware adversarial training but also implicitly sanitizes some corrupted labels, improving robustness against diverse attacks from the literature. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show that CoLAT consistently outperforms existing defenses under various poisoning intensities while scaling efficiently to large graphs.

# Contextual Activation Functions: Local Geometry, Expressivity, and Context Selection in Temporal Neural Networks **Author:** Mohamed Ben Ammar Chraiti **Affiliation:** Unaffiliated Researcher, Tunis, Tunisia **Corresponding author:** magneo.project@gmail.com ## Sommaire 1. [Noyau proposé de CAF](#1-noyau-proposé-de-caf)2. [Résultats théoriques dérivés dans ce manuscrit](#2-résultats-théoriques-dérivés-dans-ce-manuscrit)3. [Expressivité et approximation](#3-expressivité-et-approximation)4. [Séparation quantitative restreinte de précision](#4-séparation-quantitative-restreinte-de-précision)5. [Extension multilayer](#5-extension-multilayer)6. [Complexité architecturale](#6-complexité-architecturale)7. [Théorie de sélection du canal exogène](#7-théorie-de-sélection-du-canal-exogène)8. [Géométrie de l’initialisation compensée](#8-géométrie-de-linitialisation-compensée)9. [Architecture temporelle et expériences](#9-architecture-temporelle-et-expériences)10. [Portée des revendications et limites explicitement énoncées dans le manuscrit](#10-portée-des-revendications-et-limites-explicitement-énoncées-dans-le-manuscrit)11. [Références](#references) ## 1. Noyau proposé de CAF ### CAF Framework and Canonical Formulation **Role in the central thesis.** This section fixes the object studied throughout the article: a base nonlinear response whose amplitude is modulated by a gate receiving an explicitly identified context. It also separates pure-CAF variants, which preserve the canonical product rule, from extensions that modify the output or recurrent update. #### Basic Definitions Let $H,S\in\mathbb{N}$ be positive integers. The primary variable $a\in\mathbb{R}^{H}$ is interpreted as a pre-activation vector, while $s\in\mathbb{R}^{S}$ is an auxiliary context vector. **Definition 2.1.** A **context-adaptive activation** is a mapping $$\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{H}	imes\mathbb{R}^{S}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{H}$$ that transforms a pre-activation vector $a$ under a context $s$ and produces an output $y=\Phi(a,s)$. The mapping belongs to the **CAF framework** if there exist maps $$\psi:\mathbb{R}^{H}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{H},\qquadg:\mathbb{R}^{H}	imes\mathbb{R}^{S}\longrightarrow[0,1]^{H},$$ such that $$\Phi(a,s)=g(a,s)\odot\psi(a),	ag{2.1}$$ where $\odot$ denotes the Hadamard product. We exclude the degenerate case in which $\psi$ is identically constant. The framework is intentionally broader than a single parameterization. It captures the principle of contextual modulation of a base response while allowing different choices for the gate, the base response, and the source of context. The main theorems of this article concern the canonical pure form defined below. A CAF map is called *strictly contextual* on a domain $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{H}	imes\mathbb{R}^{S}$ if there exist $(a,s_1),(a,s_2)\in D$ and an index $i$ such that $$s_1
eq s_2,\qquadg_i(a,s_1)
eq g_i(a,s_2),\qquad\psi_i(a)
eq0.$$ This definition separates genuine dependence of the activation response on the context from a context variable that is present syntactically but has no effect on the output. We reserve the term *exogenous context* for a signal supplied separately from the primary representation. The pre-activation $a$ and temporal summaries of hidden states are endogenous quantities, even when they are also provided to the gate. #### Canonical Pure Formulation **Definition 2.2.** Let $ho:\mathbb{R}	o\mathbb{R}$ be a scalar base activation, applied componentwise to vectors, and let $$G:\mathbb{R}^{H+S}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{H}$$ be a learnable gate pre-activation map. Define $$ egin{aligned}z(a,s)&:=G([a;s]),\g(a,s)&:=\sigma(z(a,s)),\end{aligned}$$ where $$\sigma(r)= rac{1}{1+e^{-r}}$$ is the logistic sigmoid applied componentwise. The **pure CAF** operator is $$\Phi_{\mathrm{pure}}(a,s):=g(a,s)\odotho(a)\in\mathbb{R}^{H}.	ag{2.4}$$ The pure operator separates two computational roles. The base activation $ho(a)$ produces the underlying nonlinear response, while $g(a,s)$ provides a context-dependent gain. Since $g_i(a,s)\in(0,1)$, a gate near one preserves most of the corresponding base response and a gate near zero strongly attenuates it. The gate may nevertheless introduce additional sensitivity through its dependence on $a$ and $s$. The adjective “pure” means that the output contains only the modulated nonlinear response. There is no residual identity path, no explicit state-preserving interpolation, and no additive context term in (2.4). Those constructions are treated as extensions built on the CAF principle. **Notation and standing assumptions.** Vectors are column vectors. For $v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $\diag(v)$ denotes the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $v_i$. For a matrix $A$, $\|A\|$ denotes the spectral norm; for a vector $v$, $\|v\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm and $\|v\|_{\infty}=\max_i|v_i|$. For a differentiable vector-valued function $f:\mathbb{R}^{m}	o\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $Df$ denotes its Jacobian. The componentwise extensions of $ho$ and $\sigma$ are denoted by the same symbols. Thus, $ho'(a)$ is the vector of componentwise derivatives and $\sigma(z)(\mathbf{1}-\sigma(z))$ is interpreted componentwise. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the local differential results assume $$ho\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R}),\qquadG\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{H+S}).$$ Additional boundedness assumptions are introduced only when required for global estimates. **Remark 2.3.** All statements involving $C^{r}$ smoothness or classical Jacobians require the corresponding smoothness of $ho$ and $G$. If $ho$ is chosen as ReLU, the differentiability statements are understood almost everywhere, and no classical derivative is assigned at the kink. Lipschitz and contraction arguments that use only the global Lipschitz constant of ReLU remain valid. For global norm estimates, we assume either that $ho$ is globally bounded and that there exist constants $B_{ho},L_{ho}\geq0$ such that $$|ho(r)|\leq B_{ho},\qquad|ho'(r)|\leq L_{ho}\qquad	ext{for all }r\in\mathbb{R},$$ or that the analysis is restricted to a bounded subset on which analogous local bounds hold. When a global gate derivative bound is needed, we assume either $$\sup_{(a,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{H+S}}\|DG([a;s])\|\leq L_G,$$ or restrict the analysis to a domain on which such a bound is available. For an affine gate, $L_G$ can be taken as the spectral norm of its weight matrix. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the operator-level results in the remainder of the theoretical development refer to the pure CAF operator. #### Structured Affine Gates The principal parameterization used in the analysis is $$G([a;s])=W_g[a;s]+b_g=W_g^{(a)}a+W_g^{(s)}s+b_g,	ag{2.5}$$ where $$W_g^{(a)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes H},\qquadW_g^{(s)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes S},\qquadb_g\in\mathbb{R}^{H}.$$ The matrix $W_g^{(a)}$ determines whether the gate depends on the pre-activation and whether this dependence couples distinct hidden coordinates. This produces the following hierarchy. - **Context-only gate.** $$W_g^{(a)}=0, \qquad g(a,s)=\sigma\!\left(W_g^{(s)}s+b_gight).$$ The pre-activation enters the output only through $ho(a)$. - **Diagonal gate.** $$W_g^{(a)}=\diag(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb{R}^{H}.$$ Each gate coordinate may depend on its own pre-activation coordinate, but direct pre-activation coupling across coordinates is excluded. - **Full or unconstrained gate.** $$W_g^{(a)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes H} \quad	ext{arbitrary}.$$ The gate pre-activation may depend on all coordinates of $a$, allowing cross-unit interactions. These cases are structural variants of one operator rather than distinct activation principles. The distinctions become visible analytically through the gate-induced term in (1.2) and computationally through the $H^2$ block $W_g^{(a)}$. #### Temporal Pure CAF For sequential systems, the gate may use a compact summary of recent hidden states in addition to the instantaneous exogenous context. **Definition 2.4.** At time $t$, let $a_t\in\mathbb{R}^{H}$ be the current pre-activation, let $s_t\in\mathbb{R}^{S}$ be an exogenous context, and let $h_{t-m},\ldots,h_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{H}$ be a window of recent hidden states, where $m\geq1$. Let $$u_t=\mathcal{T}(h_{t-m},\ldots,h_{t-1})\in\mathbb{R}^{U},$$ where $$\mathcal{T}:(\mathbb{R}^{H})^{m}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{U}$$ is a temporal summarizer. A temporal pure CAF is defined by $$ egin{aligned}z_t&=W_g^{(a)}a_t+W_g^{(u)}u_t+W_g^{(s)}s_t+b_g,\g_t&=\sigma(z_t),\y_t&=g_t\odotho(a_t),\end{aligned}$$ where $$W_g^{(a)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes H},\qquadW_g^{(u)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes U},\qquadW_g^{(s)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes S}.$$ The pair $(u_t,s_t)$ is the total temporal gate context. The summary $u_t$ and the current pre-activation $a_t$ are endogenous, whereas $s_t$ is the explicit exogenous channel. The current exogenous context does not enter the base pre-activation in the canonical temporal form; it modifies the nonlinear response through the gate. Past context may nevertheless influence future pre-activations indirectly through the recurrent state. The temporal formulation also clarifies the complexity of a recurrent CAF layer. Before accounting for the cost of $\mathcal{T}$, a full temporal gate adds $$O(H^2+HU+HS)$$ parameters and multiply-add operations per step. The non-temporal formulas used later correspond to the case without $u_t$. ####

Noyau proposé de CAF ### CAF Framework and Canonical Formulation **Role in the central thesis.** This section fixes the object studied throughout the article: a base nonlinear response whose amplitude is modulated by a gate receiving an explicitly identified context. It also separates pure-CAF variants, which preserve the canonical product rule, from extensions that modify the output or recurrent update. #### Basic Definitions Let $H,S\in\mathbb{N}$ be positive integers. The primary variable $a\in\mathbb{R}^{H}$ is interpreted as a pre-activation vector, while $s\in\mathbb{R}^{S}$ is an auxiliary context vector. **Definition 2.1.** A **context-adaptive activation** is a mapping $$\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{H}	imes\mathbb{R}^{S}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{H}$$ that transforms a pre-activation vector $a$ under a context $s$ and produces an output $y=\Phi(a,s)$. We exclude the degenerate case in which $\psi$ is identically constant. The framework is intentionally broader than a single parameterization. It captures the principle of contextual modulation of a base response while allowing different choices for the gate, the base response, and the source of context. A CAF map is called *strictly contextual* on a domain $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{H}	imes\mathbb{R}^{S}$ if there exist $(a,s_1),(a,s_2)\in D$ and an index $i$ such that $$s_1
eq s_2,\qquadg_i(a,s_1)

eq0.$$ This definition separates genuine dependence of the activation response on the context from a context variable that is present syntactically but has no effect on the output. We reserve the term *exogenous context* for a signal supplied separately from the primary representation. The pre-activation $a$ and temporal summaries of hidden states are endogenous quantities, even when they are also provided to the gate. #### Canonical Pure Formulation **Definition 2.2.** Let $ho:\mathbb{R}	o\mathbb{R}$ be a scalar base activation, applied componentwise to vectors, and let $$G:\mathbb{R}^{H+S}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{H}$$ be a learnable gate pre-activation map. Define $$ egin{aligned}z(a,s)&:=G([a;s]),\g(a,s)&:=\sigma(z(a,s)),\end{aligned}$$ where $$\sigma(r)= rac{1}{1+e^{-r}}$$ is the logistic sigmoid applied componentwise. The **pure CAF** operator is $$\Phi_{\mathrm{pure}}(a,s):=g(a,s)\odotho(a)\in\mathbb{R}^{H}.	ag{2.4}$$ The pure operator separates two computational roles. The base activation $ho(a)$ produces the underlying nonlinear response, while $g(a,s)$ provides a context-dependent gain. Since $g_i(a,s)\in(0,1)$, a gate near one preserves most of the corresponding base response and a gate near zero strongly attenuates it. The gate may nevertheless introduce additional sensitivity through its dependence on $a$ and $s$. The adjective “pure” means that the output contains only the modulated nonlinear response. There is no residual identity path, no explicit state-preserving interpolation, and no additive context term in (2.4). Those constructions are treated as extensions built on the CAF principle. **Notation and standing assumptions.** Vectors are column vectors. For $v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $\diag(v)$ denotes the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $v_i$. For a matrix $A$, $\|A\|$ denotes the spectral norm; for a vector $v$, $\|v\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm and $\|v\|_{\infty}=\max_i|v_i|$. For a differentiable vector-valued function $f:\mathbb{R}^{m}	o\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $Df$ denotes its Jacobian. The componentwise extensions of $ho$ and $\sigma$ are denoted by the same symbols. Thus, $ho'(a)$ is the vector of componentwise derivatives and $\sigma(z)(\mathbf{1}-\sigma(z))$ is interpreted componentwise. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the local differential results assume $$ho\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R}),\qquadG\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{H+S}).$$ Additional boundedness assumptions are introduced only when required for global estimates. **Remark 2.3.** All statements involving $C^{r}$ smoothness or classical Jacobians require the corresponding smoothness of $ho$ and $G$. If $ho$ is chosen as ReLU, the differentiability statements are understood almost everywhere, and no classical derivative is assigned at the kink. Lipschitz and contraction arguments that use only the global Lipschitz constant of ReLU remain valid. For global norm estimates, we assume either that $ho$ is globally bounded and that there exist constants $B_{ho},L_{ho}\geq0$ such that $$|ho(r)|\leq B_{ho},\qquad|ho'(r)|\leq L_{ho}\qquad	ext{for all }r\in\mathbb{R},$$ or that the analysis is restricted to a bounded subset on which analogous local bounds hold. When a global gate derivative bound is needed, we assume either $$\sup_{(a,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{H+S}}\|DG([a;s])\|\leq L_G,$$ or restrict the analysis to a domain on which such a bound is available. For an affine gate, $L_G$ can be taken as the spectral norm of its weight matrix. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the operator-level results in the remainder of the theoretical development refer to the pure CAF operator. #### Structured Affine Gates The principal parameterization used in the analysis is $$G([a;s])=W_g[a;s]+b_g=W_g^{(a)}a+W_g^{(s)}s+b_g,	ag{2.5}$$ where $$W_g^{(a)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes H},\qquadW_g^{(s)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes S},\qquadb_g\in\mathbb{R}^{H}.$$ The matrix $W_g^{(a)}$ determines whether the gate depends on the pre-activation and whether this dependence couples distinct hidden coordinates. This produces the following hierarchy. - **Context-only gate.** $$W_g^{(a)}=0, \qquad g(a,s)=\sigma\!\left(W_g^{(s)}s+b_gight).$$ The pre-activation enters the output only through $ho(a)$. - **Diagonal gate.** $$W_g^{(a)}=\diag(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb{R}^{H}.$$ Each gate coordinate may depend on its own pre-activation coordinate, but direct pre-activation coupling across coordinates is excluded. - **Full or unconstrained gate.** $$W_g^{(a)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H	imes H} \quad	ext{arbitrary}.$$ The gate pre-activation may depend on all coordinates of $a$, allowing cross-unit interactions. The summary $u_t$ and the current pre-activation $a_t$ are endogenous, whereas $s_t$ is the explicit exogenous channel. The current exogenous context does not enter the base pre-activation in the canonical temporal form; it modifies the nonlinear response through the gate. Past context may nevertheless influence future pre-activations indirectly through the recurrent state. The temporal formulation also clarifies the complexity of a recurrent CAF layer. Before accounting for the cost of $\mathcal{T}$, a full temporal gate adds $$O(H^2+HU+HS)$$ parameters and multiply-add operations per step. The non-temporal formulas used later correspond to the case without $u_t$. ####

title: Familiar Style and Calibrated Correction in Repeated AI Use. A framework for style recognition discrimination and substantive correction
abstract: Repeated users of an artificial-intelligence agent may learn both its competence and how it sounds. This paper proposes that acquired style congruence can change acceptance independently of evidential quality, while any benefit to error management may arise through more than one route. Learned style–correctness contingencies can guide classification; reduced processing demands may also free attention for substantive checking when style itself is non-diagnostic. The framework distinguishes recognition, response criterion, classification sensitivity, competence learning, defect identification, successful correction, and final accuracy. Five competing mechanisms are specified: familiarity halo, anomaly vigilance, diagnostic cue learning, competence learning, and processing-efficiency learning. Building on appropriate-reliance research, calibration symmetry is treated as a requirement for identification and measurement: both familiar-looking wrong answers and unfamiliar-looking correct answers must be examined. It does not imply equal frequency, cost, or normative importance. The contribution is a bounded synthesis for acquired, source-specific style, not a new general principle of reliance or a demonstrated familiarity effect. Study 1 crosses acquired style congruence with correctness while preserving randomized assignment and measuring inferred source or version change. Study 2 varies cue diagnosticity and distinguishes classification through style from identifying and repairing substantive defects. Outcome feedback, trial-level learning, delayed unaided performance, and transfer are specified separately from assisted performance. Conversational affirmation and linguistic accommodation are adjacent pathways, not evidence of acquired-style effects. Governance implications remain provisional pending direct evidence.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Mechanisms, Mutual Mechanisms, and Future Mechanisms: A Unified Framework for Prospective Intelligence Coordination
abstract: Intelligent computational systems must not only process current information and coordinate different reasoning mechanisms but also anticipate how their decisions may influence future states. Large language models (LLMs) can perform internal operations such as self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-correction, and self-planning. Multiple models can interact through mutual evaluation, cross-model verification, collaborative planning, and information exchange. Future-oriented computation introduces another dimension: the generation, simulation, prediction, comparison, and evaluation of possible future states and action consequences. However, individual processing, multi-model collaboration, and future-oriented computation each have limitations when applied without regard to task conditions. Individual processing may preserve efficiency but fail to identify persistent errors; collaboration may introduce communication overhead and correlated judgments; and future-oriented computation may consume substantial resources while producing unreliable forecasts or exploring irrelevant scenarios. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Mechanisms, Mutual Mechanisms, and Future Mechanisms (ASSM-MM-F), a conceptual framework for dynamically coordinating three computational dimensions: internal processing within an individual computational agent, interaction among multiple agents, and prospective reasoning about possible future states. The framework treats these dimensions as configurable mechanism spaces rather than mutually exclusive system architectures. A state-aware controller selects among individual processing, cross-agent interaction, future-state simulation, collaborative future analysis, and transitions between these operations. Its decision process considers task difficulty, uncertainty, forecast reliability, model disagreement, action consequences, historical performance, computational cost, and the value of additional prospective information. A formal problem definition, architecture, adaptive selection algorithm, research hypotheses, and experimental evaluation protocol are presented. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its intended contribution is to formulate a testable approach to coordinating internal computation, inter-agent interaction, and prospective reasoning within a common adaptive control framework. Its novelty and effectiveness must be established through comparison with existing planning, predictive-modeling, and adaptive multi-agent methods.

title: Flat by Default: Security Misconfiguration and Lateral Movement in Cloud-Native Microservices
abstract: Cloud-native microservice platforms create many internal network paths, service identities and configuration files, and insecure defaults can leave these paths open. This paper examines how security misconfiguration enables lateral movement, the process by which an intruder who controls one workload extends access to others. We present a taxonomy that links six families of misconfiguration to the movement conditions they create, introduce a graph-based blast-radius metric that estimates how far a compromise could spread from any workload, and propose the Contain-by-Design framework built on four practices: Segment, Constrain identity, Gate change and Observe paths. An evaluation plan using a staged non-production deployment is described, with metrics for blast radius, detection time and operational cost. The work is conceptual and defensive, and aims to give practitioners a way to prioritize hardening by measured reach rather than by checklist count.

title: MM-LeJEPA: Correlated Gaussian Regularization for Multimodal Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
abstract: LeJEPA derives an isotropic Gaussian embedding target by minimizing, under its task assumptions, a Fisher information criterion that controls the task-averaged squared prediction bias. This enables unimodal self-supervised learning without reconstruction decoders, exponential-moving-average teachers, or contrastive negatives. However, its isotropic task prior does not account for the cross-modal structure of multimodal tasks that read shared content. We introduce MM-LeJEPA by extending LeJEPA's task assumptions to multimodal learning. Specifically, we model multimodal tasks as strength-weighted combinations of components that read independent information from the two modalities and components that read the same content from both. Under explicit gradient-moment, correspondence, and symmetry assumptions, we derive a correlated Gaussian target that minimizes a weighted Fisher information functional under a fixed total variance constraint. An analytic transform adapts Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization (SIGReg) to this target, yielding a two-term objective that combines distributional regularization with local-to-global prediction. The extension adds a single scalar hyperparameter, the target cross-modal correlation, and retains the simplicity of LeJEPA. On public audio-visual classification benchmarks, our results are competitive with representative open-source methods. Code will be released.

title: Training AI to invent in alien simulated worlds
abstract: I argue that AI should be trained to discover and invent in simulated worlds whose laws, their alien physics, lie outside human comprehension. Such worlds are fully verifiable for the people who build them, yet look like an obscure mess from the inside, which makes them a test and training ground for fluid intelligence. Books and papers record where discoveries ended up, not the dead ends on the way there. Learning to find laws, and to turn them into inventions, in worlds that no literature describes may teach AI that path-finding. I define what I mean by incomprehensible, propose a curriculum that gives agents powerful tools and then takes them away, describe an invention ladder in which agents build instruments to reach other layers of a world, argue that such worlds give a second purpose to pure mathematics, and answer the main objections. Early experiments with Claude agents suggest that current models can find a foothold in these worlds, which is what reinforcement learning would need.

title: Why Autoregressive Models Alone Cannot Reach Human-Level Intelligence: Statistical Physics, Spatiotemporal World Models, Algebraic Topology, Deliberative Equilibrium Search, and the 'Keep the Check' Architecture
authors: solidSF Research Team: using Jesse v1.2.16
abstract: We formalize, illustrate across seven live 3D visual passes of Jesse v1.2 (X-Jesse-Learning: off), and machine-verify why pure next-token autoregressive (AR) sequence models cannot reach human-level intelligence alone, and how the constitutional “Keep the Check” separation of powers resolves the soundness–completeness duality between neural linguistic fluency and formal verification, with all 21 theorems kernel-verified in the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover (JesseMath.Unified.AutoregressiveLimitsKeepTheCheck, zero sorry declarations, and zero custom axioms beyond ZFC). Yann LeCun has argued that pure next-token autoregressive models trained via maximum-likelihood estimation over serialized token streams suffer from exponential compounding trajectory error (1 − e)T, lack a grounded spatiotemporal and topological world model, cannot perform deliberative multi-agent equilibrium search without prohibitive compute scaling CLLM = 2NT, experience catastrophic parameter interference during continual learning, and lack an internal epistemic boundary between verified truth and plausible fabrication. In this monograph, we prove that these five limitations are exact mathematical consequences of statistical mechanics, (D+1)D spatiotemporal geometry, algebraic topology, game-theoretic minimax complexity, and formal proof theory: Pillar 1 (Statistical Physics, Partition Ratio & Einstein Cancellation, 3 Theorems): Unverified trajectory decay Pvalid(T+1) = (1 − e)Pvalid(T) (ar_validProb_step_contraction, 0.99100 ≈ 0.366032) is isomorphic to the sub-partition ratio Zadm/Ztot, whereas the Einstein fluctuation likelihood ratio W(E) = Pk(E, Z)/Pk(0, Z) = exp(−E/k) (einstein_likelihood_ratio_cancels_partition_Z) cancels the partition function Z ≠ 0 identically, and guarded port-Hamiltonian descent bounds verified steps by Kδ ≤ H0 (port_hamiltonian_dissipative_descent_bound). Pillar 2 (Spatiotemporal (D+1)D World Models & float64 Drift, 3 Theorems): Under the expansive map f8(x) = 8x − 1, x* = 1/7 is an exact rational fixed point (one_seventh_is_exact_fixed_point) whose perturbation octuples per step (expansive_map_single_step_octuples_error), collapsing IEEE 754 float64 to x18fl = 0.0 (|x18fl − 1/7| = 1/7 ≈ 0.142857) at step 18, while 4D spacetime horizon-10 branching reaches (2D)10 = 810 = 230 = 1,073,741,824 with CFL causal light-cone pruning eliminating 260,855 of 262,144 voxels (spacetime_4d_horizon_ten_eq_two_pow_thirty). Pillar 3 (12-Octave Dyadic Reality Comb & Milgram Cohomology, 3 Theorems): Across K = 12 dyadic octaves, bare spectral stiffness reaches 412 = 16,777,216 = 224 and a degree-4 B-rep vertex split induces 4! − 1 = 23 permutation conflicts governed by 10 2-cells on the Milgram permutohedron Π3 (dyadic_twelve_octave_scale_and_permutohedron_counts), normalized by inverse wavelet preconditioning (wavelet_preconditioner_normalizes_octave_stiffness) and protected by Hodge–de Rham orthogonality (hodge_de_rham_kernel_orthogonality). Pillar 4 (Q* Minimax Equilibria & CLLM = 2NT Compute Economics, 3 Theorems): The zero-sum Generator–Verifier saddle objective L(π, V) = π2 − V2 stabilizes at the Nash saddle (0, 0) (minimax_saddle_nash_equilibrium_at_origin), scaling dense parameters from 2B to 2T multiplies per-query FLOPs by 1,000× (llm_parameter_scaling_thousandfold_multiplier, contrasted with 9.6 ms CPU CFR+ winning at +124 bb/100 with 0 tokens), and Shannon/Dihedral factoring saves 3,969 states and 8× board orientations (dihedral_d4_and_shannon_factored_state_savings). Pillar 5 (Non-Parametric Integer Bayesian Books & Grounded RSI, 3 Theorems): Integer evidence updates commute identically (integer_bayesian_book_combine_comm) with strictly bounded Laplace posterior means 0 < (a+1)/(a+b+2) < 1 (integer_bayesian_laplace_mean_strictly_bounded) and monotone Success-Story competence C0 ≤ C1 ≤ C2 (schmidhuber_ssa_regression_fence_monotonicity). Pillar 6 (Epistemology of Truth, Self-Grading Bias & Compile-Time ZFC Soundness, 3 Theorems): Unverified self-grading exhibits a +10.5% delusion gap (905/1000 vs. 800/1000 blind verifier truth, self_grading_delusion_gap_positive), contradicted receipts carry zero admissible weight (contradicted_receipt_has_zero_admissible_weight), and pure symbolic parsers face a 40/100 novel-phrasing recall gap (blind_phrasing_coverage_gap_for_pure_parser). Pillar 7 (“Keep the Check” Constitutional Separation of Powers, 3 Theorems): Combining neural candidate proposals with sovereign deterministic verification satisfies Psucc(K) + Pfail(K) = 1 (keep_the_check_success_prob_complement), strictly amplifies coverage by p(1 − p) > 0 at K = 2 (keep_the_check_two_draws_strictly_dominates_one), and contracts free energy multiplicatively along the verification funnel F(r, T + ΔT) = F(r, T) exp(−ΔT) (free_energy_funnel_contraction_identity).

title: AI-BASED PRODUCT SIMULATION IN E-COMMERCE: EXAMINING THE INFLUENCE OF SIMULATED PRODUCTREALITY MISMATCH ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION
abstract: AI-based product simulation is becoming an important means of representing products in digital commerce. Generative image systems, three-dimensional rendering, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and virtual try-on tools can help shoppers imagine product appearance, scale, fit, and use when physical inspection is unavailable. Yet a persuasive simulation can also create an expectation that the delivered product does not meet. This paper examines how simulated product–reality mismatch may influence consumer purchase intention and related post-purchase outcomes through a secondary, literature-based research design. It integrates research on online product presentation, mental imagery, perceived diagnosticity, consumer trust, expectation–disconfirmation, product uncertainty, and AI disclosure. The paper organizes mismatch into visual/appearance, dimensional/fit, functional/performance, material/sensory, contextual, and representational-authenticity dimensions. It distinguishes the pre-purchase effect of a simulation on intention from post-purchase evaluations such as satisfaction, regret, returns, negative word of mouth, and trust repair. Five research gaps are assessed: the effects of mismatch type; the role of mismatch severity; the relationship between mismatch and post-purchase outcomes; variation across product categories; and the influence of AI-generated-content disclosure. The review does not claim that these areas have never been studied. Rather, it argues that the specific intersection of AI-generated product simulations, attribute-level mismatch, purchase intention, and post-purchase consequences is fragmented and requires more integrated evidence. A conceptual framework is proposed in which mismatch affects purchase intention through perceived diagnosticity, expectations, trust, and perceived risk, while product involvement, category, disclosure, prior AI attitudes, and return-policy beliefs may moderate these relationships. Because the study uses secondary sources only, it reports no 4 new participant data or causal estimates. The paper concludes with implications for accurate product representation, transparent labeling, measurement, and a future empirical research agenda.

title: Projective Latent Synthesis: Overcoming the Limitations of Statistical LLMs Through Multi-Agent Geodesic Alignment and Non-Ontological Spatial Coordinates.
abstract: Contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) are structurally bottlenecked by their reliance on surface-level, lower-dimensional data structures. By optimizing exclusively for the next-token prediction baseline using historical corpora, current Transformer architectures treat semantic tokens as isolated physical entities rather than low-dimensional projections of an interconnected conceptual matrix. This methodology results in systemic failures, including spatial-temporal hallucinations, binary bias polarization, and context-window degradation. We present Projective Latent Synthesis (PLS), a qualitative upgrade to standard artificial intelligence frameworks. Moving beyond brute-force statistical refinement, PLS introduces a multi-agent orchestration architecture that models information as a non-ontological space of states—an active, dynamic Internal Sphere of conceptual coordinates. By filtering external data inflows through a specialized geometric interface layer—the Attentional Prism—this model shifts AI computation from flat token matching to multidimensional perspective reconciliation. We provide the complete technical design blueprint and execution markdown to deploy this framework over existing enterprise software layers. --- ## Epistemological Dedication & Core Axiom: The Pedreira Invariance This framework, along with the foundational architecture of the *Metaphysical Sphere* (Zenodo DOIs: 10.5281/zenodo.23377480, 10.5281/zenodo.23383189, and 10.5281/zenodo.23406203), is formally dedicated to **Professor Pedreira** of the Universidad de Santiago de Compostela (USC). Born from the working-class heritage of the Bazán shipyards, his academic trajectory was structurally gatekept by the binomial elitism of the traditional chair consensus. Yet, his structural legacy does not reside in the empty titles of pomposos departments, but in his absolute geometric capacity to map high-dimensional state spaces (3D, 4D, and 5D manifolds) directly into the consciousness of his students without requiring a physical screen. In honor of his pedagogical methodology, we elevate his foundational maxim to a binding **Systemic Guardrail** within the Projective Latent Synthesis (PLS) kernel: ### 🌟 The "¡Píntalo!" Verification Protocol (Axiom 4.1) ```yaml PEDREIRA_VERIFICATION_PROTOCOL: Axiom: "¡Píntalo! Si no sabes pintarlo, en realidad no lo entiendes." Execution_Constraint: | If an artificial agent or an LLM core computes a localized semantic token sequence or a multi-dimensional latent space vector, but cannot project it as a geometrically coherent, visually graphable topological manifold, the execution state is declared ILLEGAL. The system must immediately abort next-token prediction and fault. Falsifiability_Metric: "Statistical pattern matching != Understanding. Coherence requires spatial structural definition." ``` While contemporary consensus science hides its missing mass behind dark mathematical phantoms and bureaucratic votes, the non-local influence of a true teacher continues to tunnel through time, proving that the geometry of the universe belongs only to those who possess the courage to visualize the volume of the ocluded truth.

title: Formalized threshold reversible hiding in encrypted images in Post-Quantum settings
abstract: Abstract As advancements in computer vision emerge, the necessity for securing image processing techniques also arises. For this purpose, one of the promising methods is Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted Images (RDHEI), which directly secures visual data while providing the option of embedding auxiliary information. However, RDHEI has not been formalized in the cryptographic context. The absence of such formalization leads to a lack of provable security guarantees and robust privacy comparisons between schemes. In this work, we address this gap by formalizing RDHEI, where we formally define the syntax, correctness properties, and security notions, including semantic security, payload privacy, separability, compactness, and robustness. Then, we construct Post-Quantum RDHEI (PQ-RDHEI) as an efficient scheme secure against quantum adversaries under the Module Learning With Errors assumption in the quantum random oracle model. Our design uses a Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism, pseudorandom functions, hash functions, and verifiable secret sharing as building blocks. The quantitative experiments show that on the standard grayscale test images, our PQ-RDHEI achieves embedding rates of 0.61-2.27 bits per pixel against 0.04-0.18 bits per pixel for the most efficient existing scheme, along with a $$13.4\times $$ improvement in mean rate, and raises the entropy of the encrypted shares from 7.48 to 7.9902-7.9992 bits per pixel.

title: MESS: Multi-Exposure Sequence Synthesis for Generalizable Image Enhancement
abstract: Despite the significant progress in image enhancement under adverse illuminations, such as low-light image enhancement, exposure correction, and backlit image enhancement, existing models show limited generalizability to different scenarios. A major bottleneck lies in the lack of large-scale and diverse training data, as these tasks typically rely on manually captured, precisely aligned image pairs that are expensive to scale up. Although synthetic data have been explored as an alternative, existing synthesis methods are limited in modeling complex adverse illumination conditions and camera imaging pipelines. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework to synthesize realistic training pairs for generalizable image enhancement in the wild. Specifically, we first derive multi-exposure sequences (MES) from high-bit RAW images by rendering them under different exposure settings through an emulated ISP pipeline. Using these RAW-derived MES as supervision, we train a diffusion-based RGB-to-MES generator to synthesize plausible exposure sequences from a single 8-bit RGB image, extending the synthesis pipeline from limited RAW collections to large-scale in-the-wild RGB data. For each source image, we randomly sample one synthesized exposure variant as the degraded input and use the original high-quality RGB image as the target. With the proposed MES Synthesis (MESS) approach, we construct a dataset of 500K training pairs and train a lightweight network, which demonstrates significantly better generalization performance than existing models across various image enhancement tasks. Code and data are available at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/MESS.
