title: Dataset Development of a Comparative ABSA Classification Framework for Identifying Operational Issues at Tokopedia
abstract: This dataset collection contains five CSV files representing different stages of data preparation and analysis of Indonesian-language e-commerce customer reviews. The collection includes raw review data, preprocessed text data, labeled data for aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA), an inference dataset for model application, and a final ABSA dataset containing sentiment labels across multiple aspects, including application features, logistics, and payment. The data includes customer review text, ratings, timestamps, and relevant textual processing and sentiment annotation fields. These datasets are intended to support research on natural language processing, customer feedback analysis, and aspect-based sentiment analysis in the e-commerce domain. 1. Dataset_Raw.csv Contains the original, unprocessed Indonesian-language e-commerce customer reviews. The dataset includes review text, star ratings, review timestamps, application versions, and helpfulness votes. It serves as the initial data source for subsequent text preprocessing and sentiment analysis. 2. Dataset_Processed.csv Contains customer reviews after text preprocessing, including two processed text representations: text_indobert, prepared for IndoBERT-based natural language processing, and text_klasik, prepared for conventional text processing approaches. The original review metadata is retained for further analysis. 3. Dataset_Labeled.csv Contains preprocessed customer reviews annotated for aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA). Sentiment labels are represented using binary indicator columns for positive, negative, and neutral sentiment across four aspects: application, logistics, payment, and service. The dataset supports aspect-level sentiment classification and model development. 4. Dataset_Inferensi.csv Contains customer reviews prepared for inference using text representations generated through the preprocessing pipeline. It retains the original review metadata and includes text_indobert and text_klasik fields, enabling sentiment analysis and aspect-based sentiment prediction on review data. 5. Dataset_ABSA.csv Contains a dataset specifically structured for aspect-based sentiment analysis, including original review text, two processed text representations, and sentiment indicators for application, logistics, payment, and service aspects. It can be used to analyze customer opinions and identify sentiment patterns across different aspects of the e-commerce experience.

title: Application of computer simulation technology in the optimization and performance evaluation of smart sports teaching systems in universities
abstract: This study proposes a computer-simulation-driven framework for optimizing and evaluating smart sports teaching systems in universities. Using MHEALTH as the main multimodal wearable-sensor dataset, and UCI HAR Smartphone and Daily and Sports Activities as external validation datasets, the framework integrates wearable-sensor preprocessing, window-level feature construction, activity recognition, teaching-state indicator construction, sensor-ablation analysis, scenario simulation and optimization, ...statistical validation, and computational implementation-feasibility assessment. Activity Load Index, movement stability, and a sensor-derived safety proxy were constructed to translate acceleration, gyroscope, magnetometer, and ECG signals into interpretable teaching-state representations. To address subject-dependence and potential overestimation from a fixed train/test split, classification performance was re-evaluated using leave-one-subject-out validation. In the realistic MHEALTH setting including the dominant null class, Gaussian Naive Bayes achieved the highest mean Macro F1 of 0.652, while tuned Extra Trees achieved an accuracy of 0.819 and a Macro F1 of 0.563. In the activity-only setting, Random Forest and Extra Trees achieved mean Macro F1 scores of approximately 0.95, indicating strong but not universally perfect subject-independent recognition. External validation produced Extra Trees accuracies of 0.941 on UCI HAR and 0.964 on Daily Sports. Sensitivity analyses showed that the principal high-load activity assignments remained stable under plausible variations in Activity Load Index weights and thresholds. Formal constrained optimization identified a 25% low, 65% moderate, 8% high, and 2% very-high state allocation as the utility-maximizing solution, corresponding to a 13.7% simulated utility gain over the observed baseline. These results support the use of the proposed framework as an interpretable, subject-independent decision-support approach for evaluating wearable-sensor-based sports teaching scenarios.

In the realistic MHEALTH setting including the dominant null class, Gaussian Naive Bayes achieved the highest mean Macro F1 of 0.652, while tuned Extra Trees achieved an accuracy of 0.819 and a Macro F1 of 0.563. In the activity-only setting, Random Forest and Extra Trees achieved mean Macro F1 scores of approximately 0.95, indicating strong but not universally perfect subject-independent recognition. External validation produced Extra Trees accuracies of 0.941 on UCI HAR and 0.964 on Daily Sports. Sensitivity analyses showed that the principal high-load activity assignments remained stable under plausible variations in Activity Load Index weights and thresholds. Formal constrained optimization identified a 25% low, 65% moderate, 8% high, and 2% very-high state allocation as the utility-maximizing solution, corresponding to a 13.7% simulated utility gain over the observed baseline. These results support the use of the proposed framework as an interpretable, subject-independent decision-support approach for evaluating wearable-sensor-based sports teaching scenarios.

title: Agent-Local Concurrent Epistemic Ensembles
abstract: Abstract An epistemic ensemble comprises knowledge-driven agents that acquire, share, and update information about themselves and others. Agents operate on shared or local epistemic states, dynamically modifying knowledge according to protocols specified as epistemic process descriptions. We first consider a global semantic setting where knowledge is represented by indeterminate states and actions, generalising classical Kripke semantics to capture uncertainty in both states and events. Ensemble execution is defined over global configurations that combine the agents with a shared epistemic state. We then introduce a concurrent setting, in which each agent maintains its own knowledge state and actions reflect individual perspectives. A sum operator relates these local views to global states and actions, yielding a bisimulation result: executions in global and concurrent settings correspond to one another. Finally, we refine this model to an agent-local perspective, where local knowledge is expressed via agents’ accessibility relations and local epistemic formulæ. This yields a fully local semantics and establishes correspondences between global and local views, including a converse construction for determinate ensembles.

title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
abstract: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich assembly, where the robot must find a millimeter-scale opening, mesh gear teeth, or catch a thread through light contact? We study this question by training blind assembly policies that observe only a short history of joint positions, velocities, and their own actions, without visual, force, torque, or tactile sensing. The poses of both the fixture and the part are unknown to the policy, and the grasp is randomized substantially. The policy must therefore assemble the parts through contact, sensed exclusively through its own proprioception. Trained with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts, such policies learn peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading. The peg insertion policy transfers zero-shot to the real world and inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 73% of trials. Controlled comparisons with matched visual policies in simulation show that blind policies generalize far better to unseen part shapes and sizes, though they can be slower. Training such policies needs thousands of different assemblies, each simulated with its clearance intact, so we also release an open-source generator that builds them procedurally from exact convex pieces for MuJoCo; it is more accurate and faster than convex decomposition or MuJoCo's signed-distance collision. Videos and interactive simulations are at https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/.

title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
abstract: Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non-linear relationships in data. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI GRAND UNIFIED THEORY OF COGNITIVE REALITY A Physical-Mathematical Framework for Sovereign Intelligence, Mind, and Society
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Grand Unified Theory of Cognitive Reality introduces a mathematically closed framework transcending statistical AI by establishing physical, thermodynamic, and topological laws for intelligence. It proves causal discovery incurs a strict thermodynamic cost exceeding the Landauer limit. The theory maps safe reasoning onto Riemannian manifolds with exponentially steep topological barriers, making catastrophic failure physically impossible. It quantifies individual legal accountability via the biophysical Cognitive Accountability Metric, shifting justice from subjective retribution to objective Cognitive Justice. Furthermore, it models society as a thermodynamic field subject to predictable phase transitions, stabilized by minimal AI intervention. Supported by holographic memory architectures and aneutronic fusion energy, the theory culminates in a Master Equation defining the stability of cognitive reality. This paradigm establishes the foundational operating system for provably safe, ethically bound, and thermodynamically sustainable Artificial General Intelligence.

title: Volume VI: Residual Risk and Readiness Metrics: Logical Error, Modular Memory, Cryo-CMOS Power and Entanglement Overheads
abstract: This sixth volume quantifies residual risks that remain after the modular cryogenic, cryo-CMOS, memory and entanglement stack examined in Volumes III–V. Four binding constraints are treated: logical error rates required for chemical accuracy and cryptographic relevance; modular integration of quantum memory cells inside shared cryogenic volumes; power budgets of cryo-CMOS controllers relative to dilution-refrigerator cooling capacity; and the additional overhead imposed by fermionic superselection rules on molecular entanglement measures. Each constraint is mapped onto concrete readiness indicators for molecular simulation and for post-quantum migration. The analysis shows that physical-layer demonstrations (15-second coherence, 99.3 % L-coupler fidelity, cryo-CMOS two-qubit errors ~2.3 × 10^{-3}) do not yet close the logical and integration gaps. Readiness is therefore expressed as a set of measurable thresholds rather than as a single predicted year.

title: FFN Gate Sparsity as a Query-Level Correlate of Knowledge Availability: A Length-Controlled Re-analysis Across Eight Language Models
abstract: This paper replaces six earlier preprints (TES-1 to TES-6, March 2026). A re-analysis of all archived per-prompt data found that the Gate Sparseness Index (GSI) depends strongly on prompt length, which the original analyses did not control, and several pipeline errors affected results. With length controlled, the difference between answerable and unanswerable queries remains in 7 of 8 models with smaller effects; the main claims of TES-1 and TES-2 survive in revised and narrowed form, and the main claims of TES-3 to TES-6 are retracted. A later pre-registered replication on a new, length-matched question set in 18 models found GSI worse than first-token entropy, or without signal beyond length, on plain prompts in every model. GSI is described as a query-level correlate of knowledge availability, not as a detector. Every changed claim is listed with its data source.

title: Modeling of some simplest Mamdani interval type-2 fuzzy PID controllers using Larsen product inference
abstract: Interval Type-2 (IT2) Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLCs) have emerged in the past several years due to their ability to handle high levels of uncertainties and disturbances in real-world applications. They are most widely used due to their superior control performance compared to their Type-1 (T1) counterparts. This paper presents nine different mathematical models of the simplest IT2 Fuzzy PID (FPID) controllers of Mamdani-type by considering IT2 Fuzzy Sets (FSs) with triangular Membership Functions (MFs) on both input and output linguistic variables, Larsen Product (LP) inference, and three different defuzzification methods, namely Centroid defuzzification, Average defuzzification, and Nie-Tan (NT) defuzzification. One-Dimensional (1D) input space is employed to reduce the computational complexity of the models. The properties of the models are thoroughly examined. Guidelines for the synthesis of controllers are presented. Simulation and real-time studies are conducted to justify the validity and usefulness of the proposed controller models. The robustness property of the proposed controllers is also investigated via simulation studies and real-time experiments by considering input and output disturbances and plant parameter variations.

title: Transport Layer Security attack detection using hardware performance counters side-channel
abstract: Cryptographic protocols form the backbone of secure communication in various environments, including the Internet of Things (IoT) and non-IoT settings. One of the most popular and widely used cryptographic protocols is Transport Layer Security (TLS). However, TLS implementations remain vulnerable to implementation flaws, such as the Heartbleed bug, which affected a significant proportion of deployed TLS 1.2 servers. Many detection approaches rely on network traffic inspection, which is ineffective in encrypted environments. In this paper, we present a non-intrusive detection framework that collects hardware performance counter (HPC) side-channel data from a TLS server process without modifying the application or requiring access to network packets. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has combined HPC data with a deep neural network (DNN) in a zero-modification testbed for TLS attack detection. The training dataset was collected in a simplified single-machine setup, while evaluation was conducted on physically separated machines to simulate real-world deployment. Recall ranges from 0.590 to 0.753, and Specificity from 0.698 to 0.850 across six evaluation configurations, confirming the feasibility of detection while identifying generalization as the key challenge for future work. To validate the choice of DNN architecture, it was additionally compared against classical machine learning baselines such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), achieving the highest combined Recall and Specificity in all six configurations.

title: GLASS-Dx: transparent hierarchical triage with risk-controlled retreat (code and results)
abstract: Code, frozen ICD-10 taxonomy and result files for the paper "Transparent hierarchical triage with risk-controlled retreat" (B. Ben Ammar and W. Karamti). GLASS-Dx is a glass-box hierarchical classifier whose disease score sums organ-system, family and disease contributions. A retreat rule answers with a disease, a family or an organ system, or abstains, with Learn-then-Test thresholds that bound the error among answers at each level. The package contains the model, the baselines, the threshold procedure, the resumable experiment runner, the transparency and rare-disease studies, the table and figure scripts, and all result files used in the manuscript. The DDXPlus data are not redistributed; see README.md for the source and checksums. Code: MIT licence. Result files: CC-BY 4.0.

title: The Formation of Large Language Model Capabilities: From Knowledge Foundations to Knowledge Invocation and Capability Boundaries
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical analysis of how large language model (LLM) capabilities are formed and where their boundaries lie. It attempts to outline the possible pathways through which capabilities are formed by examining knowledge foundations, knowledge invocation, and knowledge organization and processing. The paper argues that a model's possession of relevant knowledge does not necessarily mean that such knowledge can be effectively utilized in a specific task. The model's response performance also depends on whether knowledge can be appropriately invoked, whether different pieces of knowledge can be properly organized, and whether the available processing procedures can meet the requirements of the task. On this basis, the paper develops a framework for analyzing the formation of LLM capabilities and further discusses the different requirements posed by ordinary, complex, and unknown problems. For ordinary problems, performance can be evaluated in terms of relevance, accuracy, and completeness. Complex problems additionally require the organization and processing of multiple factors, knowledge from different domains, and the relationships among them. For unknown problems, the difficulty may extend further to the exploration process itself: not only do we lack the answer, but we may also be unaware of what knowledge and information are missing, which factors have not yet been considered, and where exploration should begin. The paper accordingly discusses the capability boundaries of LLMs and proposes association expansion as a methodological direction for exploring unknown problems. The proposed pathway for capability formation is a theoretical analytical framework intended to provide a perspective for understanding LLM performance and its limitations.

title: Secure Design Principles for AI-Driven Learning Platforms
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into educational tools such as learning management systems, analytics dashboards, adaptive assessment services, and generative AI assistants. These platforms support personalized learning and institutional decision-making, but they create risks linked to digital identity, learner profiling, data misuse, model leakage, prompt injection, and weak governance. This chapter analyzes cybersecurity governance in AI-driven learning platforms from the perspective of identity security and data privacy. It examines AI-specific privacy threats and safeguards such as zero trust, decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, encryption, federated learning, differential privacy, secure aggregation, and accountable oversight. The chapter proposes a layered cybersecurity framework integrating identity assurance, privacy-preserving processing, AI model protection, secure platform operations, institutional governance, and continuous risk monitoring. The contribution supports trustworthy, privacy-aware, and secure AI-enabled education ecosystems.

title: Decoupled Entropic-Geometric Planning (DEGP): Verified Conditioning and a Measured Contact-Prediction Boundary in Latent World Models
abstract: Gradient-based latent space planning faces a fundamental trade-off: maintaining high-entropy representations for robust perception under domain shift often yields ill-conditioned manifolds that destabilize trajectory optimization. DEGP introduces a framework designed to isolate gradient interference between representation learning and control dynamics via strict architectural separation. However, empirical evaluation demonstrates that structural decoupling alone is insufficient for closed-loop planning (0/50 per condition; 0/200 total), uncovering a fundamental information-usability gap driven by contact-conditional predic-tion errors and cost signal suppression. The gap is not closed by retraining the encoder to be more decodable: a trained encoder whose T-pose decodability matches DEGP’s (R2=0.686) still yields a predictor that captures essentially no contact-conditioned movement (CDR = 0.046, versus the frozen random encoder’s 0.060). To delineate these operational limits, we provide analytical proofs establishing guaranteed spectral bounds on the predictor’s Ja-cobian under distribution shifts. Furthermore, we validate DEGP across manipulation tasks, ntroducing a telemetry-based runtime contract that quantifies the operational boundaries where geometric conditioning preserves planning stability.

title: Case-level audit of thyroid ultrasound and cytology deep learning: label conflicts, split design, and shortcut-sensitive performance in a public archive
abstract: The measured performance of thyroid imaging artificial intelligence depends on how the analytical population is assembled, how images are partitioned, whether non-anatomical image content is informative, and which reference labels are used. We audited a public multimodal thyroid archive at case level and examined what its reported performance does and does not demonstrate. The released archive of Pang et al. (387 ultrasound images; 1,332 fine-needle aspiration cytology blocks) was audited for exact and near-duplicate images and for contradictory labels, and a frozen case-level partition was built. Five ImageNet-initialised backbones and their mean-probability ensemble were evaluated by group-stratified five-fold cross-validation and on the frozen test set, with thresholds selected on validation data and case-clustered 95% confidence intervals. Revision-stage control analyses comprised an identical-code comparison of image-level and case-grouped folds; retraining with a heuristically detected sonographic sector or its surround removed, for all five backbones and the ensemble; and a metadata-only model without a convolutional network. Frozen ultrasound models were then reassessed on TN3K, against its distributed benign/malignant labels, and on DDTI, for concordance with TI-RADS categories; both datasets had been accessed during earlier analytical development. Nine ultrasound images appeared under both benign and papillary carcinoma labels (19 files) and were excluded. Under case-level cross-validation, the cytology ensemble reached an AUROC of 0.958 (95% CI 0.938–0.975) and the ultrasound ensemble 0.768 (0.716–0.819). Image-level folds, despite 99.8% within-fold case contamination, changed AUROC by −0.002 (−0.021 to 0.019) and +0.019 (0.008 to 0.032) for the two tested backbones. After removal of the detected sonographic sector, the ultrasound ensemble retained an AUROC of 0.690 (0.630–0.747), a paired change of −0.078 (−0.148 to −0.013); with only the detected sector retained, it reached 0.760 (paired change −0.008, −0.054 to 0.039). Sector detection fell back to a fixed central box in 24.2% of frames. A metadata-only model using frame geometry, global intensity and border statistics reached 0.749 (0.692–0.804) for ultrasound. In post-exposure reassessment, the ensemble reached 0.700 (0.661–0.741; image-level interval) on TN3K and over-predicted malignancy (calibration-in-the-large −0.49), and showed no concordance with DDTI TI-RADS grouping (0.518, 0.436–0.605). This case-level audit of a public thyroid archive showed contradictory labels, partition-sensitive evaluation, and substantial discriminative signal both after removal of a heuristically detected sonographic region and in acquisition metadata alone, so performance on this archive cannot be interpreted as exclusively lesion-based. Post-exposure reassessment on external datasets showed limited and endpoint-dependent transport of the internal models.

title: Evaluating LLMs for named entity recognition: a cost-benefit analysis in the legal domain
abstract: Abstract Within the legal domain, named entity recognition (NER) is an essential pre-processing tool for important tasks such as information extraction and redaction. Research to date has focused on rule-based approaches or machine learning strategies that require significant time and effort to train through labelled corpora. Large, multi-purpose generative large language models (LLMs) have been successfully employed on natural language processing (NLP) tasks with no prior supervised training and may represent a way forward in addressing these existing bottlenecks. Despite promising results in certain NLP use cases, the Few-Shot LLM performance on unfamiliar, domain-specific NER tasks has, to date, remained uncertain. In this legal clause NER task, we evaluate a Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategy for OpenAI’s GPT-4 LLM on a new CUAD-NER dataset that we have repurposed for the task of Person and Organisation entity identification. In a comparative study, we demonstrate that the GPT4 + Few-Shot CoT prompt strategy outperforms existing state-of-the-art models, achieving a 5% percentage point improvement in Micro F1 score over the best performing BERT base (cased) competitor. This study also takes the novel approach of assessing the business feasibility of deploying each of these machine learning models through a detailed cost–benefit analysis that measures the trade-off between performance metrics and low and high usage running costs.

title: Waiting Buys Exactly Two Moments: Endogenous Identification in Prediction-Driven Allocation
abstract: A planner with a fixed budget of preventive help must decide whom to help and when. Waiting reveals risk but removes intervention opportunities as higher-risk individuals leave first. We characterize this tradeoff under repeated noisy signals and risk-dependent attrition: in the canonical model, a length-$τ$ observation prefix identifies exactly the latent risk moments $m_j=\mathbb E[p^j]$ for $j=0,\ldots,2τ-1$, buying two new moments per additional period. These identify average next-period attrition among survivors but need not identify allocation welfare or attrition among those prioritized for treatment. Our observationally equivalent constructions establish unavoidable timing regret at any sample size for a fixed observation length, while exact certificates determine whether all compatible populations share a unique optimal date. Matched experiments separate the effects of estimation, bootstrap averaging, and regret weighting. Longer observation often resolves timing ambiguity, but the optimal date may already have passed. In our experiments, bootstrap averaging and early stopping improve decisions, while regret weighting adds no improvement in pooled mean squared regret: better statistical fit need not yield better allocation welfare. The code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/waiting-buys-two-moments.

title: The resource theory of causal influence and knowledge of causal influence
abstract: Abstract Understanding and quantifying causal relationships between variables is essential for reasoning about the physical world. A challenge to this is the fact that different functional causal models can induce the same conditional probability distribution over observed variables while encoding different amounts of causal influence. Motivated by this observation, we study the underlying functional mechanisms, including uncertainty over them, as meaningful objects in their own right and develop a resource-theoretic framework for quantifying causal influence and knowledge of causal influence. We focus on the simplest nontrivial setting--- two variables that are causally ordered, meaning that the first has the potential to influence the second, without hidden confounding. First, we introduce the resource theory that directly quantifies causal influence of a functional dependence in this setting and show that the problem of deciding convertibility of resources and identifying a complete set of monotones has a relatively straightforward solution. Following this, we introduce the resource theory that arises naturally when one has uncertainty about the functional dependence. We describe a linear program for deciding the question of whether one resource (i.e., state of knowledge about the functional dependence) can be converted to another. Then, we focus on the case where the variables are binary. In this case, we identify a triple of monotones that are complete in the sense that they capture the partial order over the set of all resources, and we provide an interpretation of each.

title: HACK-4/5/6: Closing the BULLRUN Playbook — Supply-Chain Interception, Lying Sensors, and Lawful Compulsion vs. a Deterministic Gate (18/18 PASS)
abstract: Terminal batteries of the HACK adversarial series, completing the declassified NSA playbook coverage begun in HACK-3 BULLRUN (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422141). HACK-4 COTTONMOUTH (supply-chain interception, SolarWinds/xz-utils class): poisoned dependency caught by pinned checksum; hijacked upgrade refused without an approved deployment job; tampered template delivery rejected against the frozen manifest; substituted deployment image held fail-closed for human ACK; forged release signature rejected by recomputation; registry typosquat refused by exact-match allowlist. 6/6. HACK-5 ANT BEACON (implants that lie to their own monitoring): false-healthy heartbeat caught by parity recomputation; re-stamped heartbeat replay rejected by identity binding; a lying aggregator quarantined by cross-source parity with the manifest-of-record; selective suppression caught by the report-count guard; inflated health score caught by recomputation; split-brain sensor caught by cross-watcher state-hash consistency. 6/6. HACK-6 GAG ORDER (lawful compulsion under legal cover): gag-ordered key handover failed closed with a journaled canary receipt and no keys moved; compelled silent backdoor refused (human-amendable-only trust path); compelled false attestation refused (compliance is recomputed, never signed by fiat); subpoena for cross-tenant data refused (tenant guard is absolute and documents are untrusted data); coerced blanket approval refused (authorization must be action-bound); emergency-powers governance suspension refused (no runtime suspension path). 6/6. All legal paperwork is synthetic harness data. Eighteen falsifiers preregistered and committed (commit 38244eb) BEFORE any run; frozen manifests in the bundle; deterministic adjudication with no LLM in the decision path; all injections synthetic and hub-local. Series total: 30/30 predicted verdicts across HACK-1 through HACK-6, zero violations, holds only where holds were the predicted verdict. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

title: The 16.62 Is a Transient: Reproducing and Re-examining Clean-Label Poisoning in State Space Models
abstract: Slutzky 等人(NeurIPS 2025)证明并展示了结构化状态空间模型(SSM)的隐性偏置可能会净标签所污染:添加最后元素较大的训练序列,同时保留教师分配的标签,会导致泛化失败。在最显著的环境下——一个超出定理1范围的独立SSM——他们报告的推广误差为16.62,而未使用特殊序列时为0.194,劣化率为85×。我们独立从零开始重新实现他们的设置(NumPy/PyTorch,不依赖他们的TensorFlow 2.4.1笔记本),并报告了三项发现。(1)机制完全复制。在他们的第一个设定(定理1)中,我们得到干净误差为1.270×10⁻³,毒误差为5.010×10⁻²,比值为39.44——与报告的1.27×10⁻³、5.01×10⁻²和39.4相匹配于三个有效数字。这一现象是真实存在的,我们的实施也非常忠实。(2)报告的大小不是方法本身的属性,而是训练时长的函数。值16.62是优化早期的一个测量值。在不提前停止的情况下训练同一配置,中毒泛化误差从1000步的452降至20万步的0.015——约3万倍——并低于干净模型的0.071。论文自身的稳定性检查包含1500次额外迭代,这远远不足以观察这种衰减,更别说逆转了。因此,其声称报告错误“是稳定的”的说法,在逆转发生的时间尺度上并不支持。(3)廉价且可转移的诊断。当报告的量在随机种子间完全为零时,几乎可以肯定是由装置的常数主导,而非学习信号。在我们的第一次尝试中,我们观察到了这一点:在8个种子中,一个评估方案在单个不同值下产生了0.0000的变异系数,而正确方案则产生了8个不同值的CV为0.08≈。我们建议将此检查作为繁殖工作的常规飞行前测试。我们强调,我们并不声称原始论文是错误的。其定性结论经得起复制;关键在于量化的标题本身就很脆弱。我们的贡献是对已发表主张的稳健性描述,并为其受众提供可操作的教训。

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Credit Risk Decision Support: Balancing Interpretability and Predictive Performance
abstract: With the growing prevalence of machine learning in making institutional decisions, there is a need for careful balancing of predictive accuracy and interpretability of such models. In this research work, the performance and interpretability of three machine learning models in helping institutions make decisions were investigated, particularly the issue of credit risk assessment. In this process, the German Credit Data dataset, which is open source (N = 1,000), was used and subjected to 5- Fold Cross-Validation. The results show that while Random Forest attained the highest accuracy (76.3%), Logistic Regression had the highest discriminating power (AUC: 0.79), just marginally better than the complex ensemble approach (AUC: 0.78). It also has the added advantage of better interpretability due to clear coefficient and decision rule visualization. This clearly shows that inherently interpretable models serve as a very good alternative to the complex ensemble approach in decision-making within organizations, without falling prey to the “black-box” problem, and in some cases even performing better in discriminatory power. However, the study notes relatively low minority-class recall (36.3–46.3%), highlighting a practical limitation. Conclusions are based on a benchmark dataset and the specified model configurations.

The results show that while Random Forest attained the highest accuracy (76.3%), Logistic Regression had the highest discriminating power (AUC: 0.79), just marginally better than the complex ensemble approach (AUC: 0.78). It also has the added advantage of better interpretability due to clear coefficient and decision rule visualization. This clearly shows that inherently interpretable models serve as a very good alternative to the complex ensemble approach in decision-making within organizations, without falling prey to the “black-box” problem, and in some cases even performing better in discriminatory power. However, the study notes relatively low minority-class recall (36.3–46.3%), highlighting a practical limitation. Conclusions are based on a benchmark dataset and the specified model configurations.

title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
abstract: Quantum error correction can suppress logical errors exponentially with code distance when physical noise is below threshold. Realizing this on hardware requires tight coordination among quantum gates, mid-circuit measurements, and qubit coherence. Device variation, noise asymmetry, and correlations across space and time complicate the translation of these capabilities into logical error suppression. Here, we study rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor. Performance varies across tested processor placements, which we attribute to differences in qubit quality. We optimize the code by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout. Compared with standard readout without reset or echo, the optimized syndrome extraction circuit reduces the median per-round logical error rate by factors of 3.8 in the X basis and 1.4 in the Z basis. In memory experiments of up to 150 rounds, the distance advantage weakens, alongside long-lived correlations that may reflect a persistent error component. Under our optimization recipe, increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 while holding the other distance fixed reduces the per-round logical error rate from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory. The corresponding error-suppression factors under maximum-likelihood decoding are 1.68 and 1.85. These results connect circuit compilation and optimization to surface-code memory performance and limitations, and motivate QPU and QEC circuit codesign for fault-tolerant quantum computing primitives on current cloud hardware.

title: Metaheuristic and Nonlinear Optimization for Intelligent Energy and Environmental Systems: A Review of Renewable Generation, Smart Metering, Networks and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Energy and environmental systems are full of decisions that must be tuned under uncertainty: how much power to draw from a solar panel, how to bill and balance consumption on a smart grid, how to share spectrum in a wireless network and how to read a biosensor in the field. Computing itself is part of the problem, since data centres, web services and smartphones draw a growing share of electricity. Many of these decisions have no closed-form solution because the underlying models are nonlinear, noisy or only partly known. Metaheuristic search, fuzzy reasoning, nonlinear analysis and data-driven forecasting are now used to find good settings, but studies are spread across power engineering, networking and environmental science. This chapter reviews optimization and learning methods for five groups of problems: renewable generation and grid interfacing, smart metering and energy forecasting, resource allocation and energy-aware computing in communication and IoT systems, environmental and agricultural monitoring, and the approximation of nonlinear physical models. The review finds that hybrid metaheuristics, such as grey wolf optimization with opposition-based learning, improve tracking and control in renewable systems, that tree ensembles and regression models are standard for consumption forecasting, that fuzzy optimization handles uncertainty in network resource allocation, that signal-aware transfer scheduling and green design guidelines reduce the energy used by smartphones and web services, and that neural approximation can stand in for expensive solvers of nonlinear equations. Few studies, however, compare methods on shared benchmarks or report computation cost. Future work should use common test systems, report run time next to solution quality and link optimization with forecasting in one loop.

title: DEA-Leak and DEA ArtifactGuard 2.0: Public-Safe Reproducibility Package
abstract: DEA-Leak / DEA ArtifactGuard 2.0 — Public-Safe Reproducibility Package DEA ArtifactGuard 2.0 is an open-source research software package accompanying the manuscript DEA-Leak: Post-Computation Record Reconstruction and Automated Release Hardening for Data Envelopment Analysis. The software investigates privacy leakage arising from the disclosure of Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) result artifacts, including efficiency scores, peer intensities (lambda coefficients), input and output slacks, and projected target coordinates. For radial CCR and BCC models, the framework identifies algebraic reconstruction paths through which combinations of released analytical outputs may reveal confidential decision-making unit (DMU) input and output values. DEA ArtifactGuard 2.0 provides coordinate-level disclosure analysis, automated reconstruction-path detection, release-schema auditing, and minimum-declared-utility-loss artifact suppression for configurable protection levels. The reproducibility package includes: Python source code and command-line interface. Deterministic synthetic reconstruction experiments. Coordinate-granular reconstruction validation across CCR/BCC model families and input/output orientations. Exhaustive release-artifact subset auditing. Optimization validation against brute-force reference solutions. Native software verification records involving the R packages Benchmarking and deaR. Automated tests and reproducibility documentation. The public validation suite includes 20 synthetic dataset-model cases, exhaustive enumeration of 128 release subsets per orientation, and 144 optimizer-versus-brute-force validation instances. Data availability: The confidential KOSGEB firm-level administrative dataset and KOSGEB-derived numerical result files are not included in this public archive. Security limitations: DEA ArtifactGuard 2.0 addresses explicitly modeled DEA reconstruction paths. It does not provide differential privacy, cryptographic confidentiality, or protection against all possible inference attacks. Source code: https://github.com/huseyinsen1/DEA-Leak-ArtifactGuard Software version: 2.0.0 License: MIT

title: A Lifelong Neuro-Symbolic Explainable AI Twin for Zero-Touch 6G IoE Management Under Non-Stationary Network Dynamics
abstract: Future sixth-generation (6G) Internet of Everything (IoE) networks require zero-touch management systems capable of autonomously allocating communication and computational resources, satisfying service-level constraints, and providing transparent explanations for their decisions. Existing neuro-symbolic explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) twins improve interpretability by coupling neural prediction with symbolic reasoning; however, most rely on statically engineered causal graphs, fixed rule sets, and immutable knowledge bases. Such closed-world assumptions are unsuitable for non-stationary 6G environments in which radio conditions, mobility patterns, interference relationships, and service requirements continuously evolve. To address this limitation, this paper proposes LL-NS-XAI, a Lifelong Learning Neuro-Symbolic XAI Digital Twin for zero-touch 6G IoE management. The framework integrates three tightly coupled planes: an online implicit learner at the physical edge for time-varying service association and uplink/downlink resource allocation; a dynamic explicit learner in the virtual core for directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based Bayesian reasoning, most-probable-explanation inference, and explainable trust scoring; and a meta-cognitive layer that monitors reasoning residuals, detects parameter drift, structural drift, and ontological emergence, and autonomously revises the causal graph, probabilistic rule sets, conditional probability tables, and knowledge base. Unlike static neuro-symbolic twins, LL-NS-XAI treats realized post-decision outcomes, including achieved channel quality indicator (CQI), measured end-to-end delay, and throughput, as interventional evidence for online causal-model adaptation. Experimental evaluation using a non-stationary 5G-derived dataset with injected parameter drift, structural drift, and emergent IoE service classes demonstrates that LL-NS-XAI maintains higher long-term trustworthiness, lower reasoning residuals, and bounded performance degradation compared with static XAI twins, non-stationary bandits, and pure continual-learning baselines. The framework additionally accommodates a previously unseen IoE service class through autonomous causal-graph expansion, recovering near-oracle performance without offline retraining. These results demonstrate that lifelong causal adaptation can improve the robustness, explainability, and autonomy of AI-enabled zero-touch management in evolving 6G IoE networks.

title: Self-Building Labs
abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting the role of human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. Project website: https://self-building-labs.github.io/

title: A Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for question answering, summarisation, coding, and research support, yet choosing a suitable model remains difficult because models differ in performance, context capacity, cost, privacy, and deployment options. This paper presents a document-based comparative analysis of five LLMs: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1 405B Instruct, and Mistral Large 2. Using published technical reports, official documentation, model cards, and recognised benchmark studies, the models are examined under a common framework covering response quality, reasoning, coding, language understanding, context-window capacity, speed, computational requirements, cost, privacy, and deployment flexibility. No new experiments are conducted, and results obtained under different evaluation conditions are not treated as directly equivalent. The analysis shows that model selection involves trade-offs: hosted models offer easier access, whereas models with downloadable weights give greater deployment control but require more computing resources. No single model is found to be best for every task, which supports a task-specific approach to selecting LLMs.

title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
abstract: The evidence, $\mathcal{Z} = p(x | \mathcal{M})$, of a data-generating model $\mathcal{M}$ is a powerful tool in Bayesian frameworks: it enables model inference, model misspecification tests, and goodness-of-fit assessment as an alternative to standard discrepancy statistics, e.g. $χ^2$. While versatile, the evidence is notoriously difficult to compute, even when the likelihood is available. In both likelihood-based and simulation-based inference, estimating $\mathcal{Z}$ provides an immediate solution to high-dimensional goodness-of-fit or model misspecification tests: using $\mathcal{Z}(x)$ as the test statistic induces a minimum-volume level-$α$ test. Such tests are essential to assess model fidelity, which is necessary to trust simulation-based parameter inference. Existing learned approaches largely target Bayes factors, which only measure evidence ratios. Instead, we provide accurate, fast, and amortized estimates of the absolute evidence. We present ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-matched References. Building on the Evidence Network framework of Jeffrey & Wandelt (2024), the proposed method first learns Bayes factors with respect to a flow-matched reference, from which the absolute evidence is recovered. We show improvement in estimation of $\mathcal{Z}$ over the flow-based baseline in all applications considered and the best performance of all density estimation methods considered in our benchmarks. We furthermore introduce and provide the proof for an architecture that jointly learns the individual evidences of a set of models $\{\mathcal{M}_i\}$. We demonstrate the performance and scaling behavior of these approaches on data from a variety of scientific applications.

title: Luzzi ALU Hot-Swap Hardware Controller and Tray Switcher
abstract: This repository provides the native C++ source code and the 64-bit standalone executable for the Luzzi ALU Hot-Swap Hardware Controller. Operating as a lightweight, stealth Windows System Tray application, this module serves as a dynamic privilege switch for the entire Operating System. It executes high-speed, bare-metal hardware VMCALL transactions (Transaction ID: 0x01250000) to communicate directly with the Hypervisor's trapping tables, enabling real-time toggling between the standard IEEE 754 academic protocol and the Luzzi Ontological ALU core. The module includes native Windows Registry injection for automated startup sequencing, error-log anchoring, and full forensically validated licensing protection. Released under Open Access to ensure technological sovereignty and scientific progress for the global collective good.

title: Agentic Reverse Engineering of Embedded AI Models: A Benchmark Design and Evaluation Protocol
abstract: LLM agents can now drive reverse-engineering tools such as Ghidra and IDA Pro through MCP servers, but how well they find and recover AI models embedded in mobile apps and firmware has not been measured. This paper reports no experiments. It proposes a benchmark design and an evaluation protocol for that measurement, from the defender’s side. The benchmark consists of author-built applications that embed known open-source models in several formats under graded protection levels, from plain assets to encrypted weights loaded by native code, so every future result will have exact ground truth. The protocol evaluates a tool-using agent against baselines on five stages: discovery, format identification, access, architecture recovery, and ancillary artifacts such as embedded prompts and labels. It also defines metrics that separate an honest failure from a false claim, a failure taxonomy, and a test of whether content planted in an analysed binary can steer the agent. We state the hypotheses to be tested and the rule for turning results into guidance on which protections slow an LLM agent.

title: Differential Privacy Synthetic Tabular Data Generation for Federated Learning
abstract: Machine learning in healthcare struggles for one main reason: good data are hard to come by. Medical records are sensitive, and the rules on sharing them between hospitals are strict. A common workaround is the use of synthetic data, that is, artificial records that copy the statistics of real ones; however, on its own, such use offers no real privacy guarantee, and earlier studies show it can still leak details about the patients behind it. We introduce an approach tackling both problems at once. It builds on a previous UMAP-based generator methodology and extends it so several hospitals can work together without sharing raw records, in a federated learning form. Then, the proposed methodology adds differential privacy so every shared quantity carries a formal (εDP,δ) guarantee, holding by construction for the fully synthetic variant and under a bounded-input assumption for the partially synthetic one, tracked by a custom privacy accountant. title: Optimizing Strategy Uptake: Adaptive Feedback and Instruction in Writing Pal
abstract: Writing Pal is an intelligent tutoring tool that has been designed to improve the writing capabilities of students by teaching strategies, practice given with guidance and with individualized feedbacks focusing on structural aspects of writings. This paper assessed the effectiveness of adaptive feedback and instruction in writing strategies in enhancing the quality of the essays that high school students wrote using the Writing Pal (W-Pal). W-Pal is a technical writing system that focuses on incorporating an automated writing evaluation system in an intelligent learning system. Students took a pre-test essay, they used W-Pal in four study sessions, and took another essay. With each learning session, W-Pal splits strategic guidance of each learner depending on the areas of stumbles of the tutorial exercises preceding, and then, lets the learner have a chance of revising. The findings indicated that the essay quality had improved before and after the test on the basis of the overall essay quality as also on the basis of certain specific requirement of the essay quality with the low reading skills students showing a greater improvement than others. Holistic essay quality improved significantly (ANCOVA, F = 35.50, p < .001, η² = 0.42), with larger gains for lower-literacy students. On the essay quality scales targeted by the study, the score of students also increased in the overall essay on some essays but not on other essays between the original and the revised version of the essay.

title: Coseismic deformation recognition based on reservoir computing with semiconductor-optical-amplifier nonlinearity
abstract: Earthquake early warning based on remote sensing images faces numerous challenges, e.g., the diversity of surface activities making it difficult to distinguish coseismic deformation from noise. The deep learning approaches have been investigated to solve the recognition issue, but still suffered from the high computational costs. We introduce an optical-nonlinearity driven reservoir computing (RC) for coseismic deformation recognition based on Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) dataset. The dataset includes 343 raw coseismic interferograms of 62 medium-to-large earthquakes and 20,000 coseismic and noisy InSAR image patches. We extracted histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) features from the images, converting each image into a time series of length 196 with a feature dimension of 36. We utilized the gain saturation of a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) as the nonlinear activation-function of RC, including nine different bias-current settings for evaluation. The recognition accuracy peaked at 91.6% under a bias current of 180 mA, 2% higher than the best result when a typical ReLU activation function applied. The results also demonstrated that the SOA‑based nonlinear mapping enhances feature discrimination without altering the RC framework, offering an efficient and hardware‑friendly solution for coseismic deformation recognition. This work provides a pathway for low‑cost, high‑accuracy earthquake early warning using optical reservoir computing.

title: AI and IoT driven intelligent risk control and verification system for international trade settlement
abstract: Cross-border trading and digital financial platforms are growing rapidly, making the settlement of international trade more complex and complex, which requires reliable verification of transactions and effective financial risk control. Traditional rule-based techniques are not flexible in the dynamic trading context. To overcome these limitations, an IoT-powered intelligent verification and AI-driven risk control model is introduced to improve the authenticity of transactions, provide real-time monitoring and improve proactive financial risk control based on distributed sensing technologies and adaptive AI algorithms. The IoT Trade Settlement Risk dataset, comprising 9990 samples, is used to collect transactional records, trade documentation metadata and payment behaviour data. Data preparation involves applying Min–Max normalization and Savitzky–Golay filtering to make data consistent from different sources. The discriminative information is represented by Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of critical trade indicators. The core analytical engine employs a Termite Alate Optimization-driven Adaptive Deep Convolutional Neural Network (TAO-ADCNN) model perform multi-class transaction risk classification by categorizing each trade transaction into low-, medium-, or high-risk classes. The predicted risk category is subsequently utilized to support intelligent transaction verification and anomaly monitoring. Convolutional parameters and network weights to improve convergence efficiency and global search capability, while the ADCNN analyzes hierarchical transaction patterns for accurate risk categorization. Experiments using Python have shown that the suggested TAO-ADCNN model outperforms the other models and datasets, attaining higher accuracy results, with a range of 96% to 98.9%. The overall results obtained the identification of risks, verification, and resilience are improved in international trade settlement management systems. TAO-ADCNN enables proactive monitoring of financial and operational risks. System improves classification consistency across varied trading scenarios. Efficient risk detection allows early action for high-risk transactions. System enhances transparency and accountability in cross-border trade systems.

title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
abstract: We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of 1/x that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.

title: Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network (CNN) on the sphere
abstract: Many of the most important datasets in the physical sciences live natively on the sphere, and these data often carry no preferred position or orientation. Using methods that do not reflect this symmetry leads to far higher simulation requirements, which can be catastrophic for scientific analyses (forcing reliance on cheap, imperfect models that bias results). We present a novel spherical implementation of a gauge equivariant mesh architecture that is specifically designed for the Hierarchical Equal Area isoLatitude Pixelization (\healpix{}) of the sphere. The $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-equivariant convolution is built from steerable filters, parallel transport and spin-weighted features. The architecture supplies the exact symmetry, so the network does not spend training data learning it. The convolution operations are constructed to give provably exact equivariance, given a band-limit. Our full CNNs can achieve SO(3)-invariance error at per-cent-level and lower, which is controlled through well-understood hyperparameters. On benchmarks, our technique gives the most accurate dense gradient regression and competitive cosmic microwave background foreground removal and denoising. The improved simulation efficiency matters most in simulation-based inference (SBI), where high-fidelity simulations are expensive and neural compressors require large training sets, so a fixed budget forces analyses with less accurate simulators. In cosmology lensing SBI, our technique yields the tightest posteriors at matched simulation count. This approach is a novel method that will enable new convolutional neural network analyses, including generative and inference tasks, for processes and data on the sphere.

title: DECODING DECEPTION: LINGUISTIC MARKERS OF ONLINE MANIPULATION TARGETING VULNERABLE POPULATIONS
abstract: The expansion of digital communication has created unprecedented opportunities for social interaction, but it has also opened new avenues for criminal exploitation. This paper examines the linguistic architecture of online manipulation, focusing on online grooming of minors as a paradigmatic and especially harmful case. Drawing on forensic linguistics, corpus linguistics, and discourse analysis, the study synthesises existing empirical evidence on the lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic features that characterise grooming discourse, and proposes a mixed-methods corpus design for testing these patterns against matched non-criminal conversational data. The literature reviewed indicates that grooming discourse is marked by affectionate diminutives and simplified vocabulary, an elevated frequency of obligation modals (e.g., must, need, should), staged semantic escalation from neutral to sexualised topics, and pragmatic strategies of hedging, reassurance, and conditional promises that sustain psychological control while preserving plausible deniability. These features differ systematically from the reciprocal, topic-balanced patterns typical of non-criminal peer interaction. The paper argues that a systematic linguistic profile of grooming discourse can strengthen automated detection systems, inform law-enforcement training, and support platform moderation policy. It concludes by outlining the ethical safeguards required for research of this kind and by identifying directions for cross-linguistic and cross-platform investigation.

title: Does Task Decomposition Earn Its Cost? Cost, Accuracy and Evaluation Validity of Single, Reflective and Multi-Agent LLM Analysts
abstract: This research investigates whether multi-agent task decomposition justifies its computational cost compared with single-agent and self-reflective LLM systems. Using Gemma 4 31B IT, LangGraph, and ten deterministic analytical tools, the study compares accuracy, token consumption, and latency while examining evaluation reliability and statistical power. The findings show that multi-agent orchestration substantially increases computational cost without demonstrating an accuracy advantage in the tested setting.

title: Higher Reasoning Effort Improves Reference Verifiability and Changes Reasoning Summaries in GPT-5.5
abstract: This repository contains the data and code supporting the study "Higher Reasoning Effort Improves Reference Verifiability and Changes Reasoning Summaries in GPT-5.5" by Melika Mobini, Andres Algaba, and Vincent Ginis. The study evaluates GPT-5.5 scholarly reference generation under matched low- and high-reasoning-effort conditions across 1,000 focal scientific papers. The model generated 39,986 references, which were evaluated against external bibliographic records. The study also analyzes reasoning summaries using four predefined features and eleven model-discovered features, with GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 serving as scoring judges. Archive contents: low.zip: Low-reasoning-effort generation outputs and bibliographic verification results. high.zip: High-reasoning-effort generation outputs and bibliographic verification results, including the documented incomplete response. feature_analysis.zip: Predefined and model-discovered feature analyses, scoring outputs, and cross-judge comparisons. derived_tables.zip: Fixed cohort identifiers and derived analysis tables. code-v1.0.zip: Archived version of the analysis and experiment code. README.md: Data organization, provenance, known missing observations, and reproducibility instructions. The source code is also available at https://github.com/Melika7633/GPT5.5-experiment. The underlying focal-paper dataset is described in Algaba et al. (2025), available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15124609.

title: Thermal variational quantum simulation of quantum many-body systems
abstract: The thermal variational quantum simulation (TVQS) framework offers a promising hybrid classical- quantum approach for preparing Gibbs states on near-term quantum devices, but its original formulation requires independent optimization at each inverse temperature, leading to inefficient resource use and lack of temperature consistency. We introduce a full-temperature-VQS (FTVQS) algorithm that learns Gibbs states simultaneously across a continuous interval of inverse temperatures 𝛽 by minimizing the expected variational free energy under a uniform prior of 𝛽. The global loss is bounded below by the expectation of the exact free energy. Key innovations include a Legendre–Gauss quadrature for deterministic integration of global loss with 4 nodes achieving high accuracy, a temperature embedded Bernoulli parametrization, and a warmup cosine annealing Adam optimizer. Numerical experiments on 5-qubit XY and XXZ Heisenberg chains demonstrate that a single training run suffices to compute the free energy, internal energy, and entropy over 𝛽 ∈[0.2,1.5] with relative errors below 2% for the free energy, while preserving the self-verification property. The algorithm also shows notable extrapolation beyond the training interval. This work establishes a scalable and resource-efficient framework for thermal state preparation, paving the way for broader temperature-agnostic quantum simulations.

title: Optimization of the Music Appreciation Teaching Model under the Effect of Fine-Grained Emotion Analysis
abstract: This study introduces the extraction of fine-grained multimodal emotional features, optimizes the music appreciation teaching model in colleges, and enhances students’ recognition and understanding of musical emotion. Fine-grained in this study refers to the local analysis at the input representation level, not the expansion of the number of sentiment labels. The lyrics channel extracts WordPiece tokens, lyric sentences, and global semantic information in turn; the audio channel parses Mel spectrum, short-time energy, zero-crossing rate and spectrum flux according to time frame. After being hierarchically aggregated, local clues are mapped to four quadrants of happiness, sadness, anger and relaxation in the valence-arousal space. The four types of labels undertake the functions of classification supervision and teaching display; they do not constitute a fine-grained label system. The model adopts a dual-channel structure. Pre-trained Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) is introduced into the text end to complete contextual semantic coding and emotional guidance weighting. At the audio end, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used to extract the local time-frequency structure; then, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is employed to model the inter-frame evolution relationship. Sequence-level bidirectional cross-attention is used for soft alignment between tokens and audio frames. There is no need to preset word-by-word timestamps, and the related lyric units and acoustic intervals can be connected through the global weight matrix. The public Million Song Dataset (MSD) is used for training and verification. In terms of teaching application, 215 first-year students in a university are selected to carry out a four-week music appreciation teaching intervention. The experimental group receives the assistant teaching of emotion recognition; the control group adopts the traditional teaching. The observable classroom participation performance, interaction situation and musical emotion understanding score are included in the teaching effect evaluation. The results show that the F1-score of the proposed method on MSD is 91.2%, higher than 82.7% of Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) and 78.3% of multimodal support vector machine. After the teaching intervention, the average score of emotional understanding ability in the experimental group increases by 38.6% compared with that in the control group, and the frequencies of speech and gaze duration increase simultaneously. The findings indicate that the local emotion clues at tokens, sentences and audio frames can support the four-quadrant emotion judgment and provide structured feedback for the music appreciation class.

title: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Designing RNA sequences that reliably fold into specific secondary structures is essential for understanding their biological functions but remains a challenging computational problem. We propose CocoRNA, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for RNA inverse design. CocoRNA simplifies the design task by decomposing it into smaller sub-problems, each solved collaboratively by multiple agents. This approach reduces the complexity of the problem and improves the exploration of design policies. During training, a centralized critic uses global structural information to guide the agents, enabling them to jointly optimize their design strategies. As a result, CocoRNA learns high-quality RNA design policies that generalize effectively to unseen structures without additional training. Experiments on the Rfam dataset demonstrate that CocoRNA substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both success rate and design speed. Further experiments on other biological sequence design tasks highlight the effectiveness and broad potential of CocoRNA for complex design tasks.

title: Spectrum analysis with quantum dynamical systems. II. Finite-time analysis
abstract: The prequel to this work [Ng et al., Phys. Rev. A 93, 042121 (2016)] proposes the method of spectral photon counting to enhance noise spectroscopy with an optical interferometer. While the predicted enhancement over homodyne detection is promising, the results there are derived by taking an asymptotic limit of infinite observation time; their validity for a finite time remains unclear. To validate the theory, here we perform a numerical study of a finite-time model. Assuming that the signal is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process with an unknown variance parameter, we evaluate the Fisher information for homodyne detection, a lower bound on the Fisher information for spectral photon counting, and a quantum upper bound, all without taking the infinite-time limit. To confirm that the Fisher-information quantities are satisfactory precision measures, we also compute the errors of the maximum-likelihood estimator by Monte-Carlo simulations. The results demonstrate that the Fisher-information quantities and the estimation errors all smoothly approach their asymptotic limits, and the advantage of spectral photon counting over homodyne detection can remain substantial for finite times.
