title: Varun-SV/Cascade-AI: v0.83.0
abstract: <!-- One `### Added` / `### Changed` / `### Fixed` per release, not per PR. The release workflow copies this whole block verbatim into the GitHub release notes (.github/workflows/release.yml), so appending a fresh heading per merge ships a release page with four "Added" sections — which is what happened to 0.69.0. Add bullets under the existing heading. RENAME THIS HEADING to `## - ` in the same commit that bumps package.json. The workflow matches sections by version prefix, so a bumped version with the heading still reading "Unreleased" matches nothing — which is how 0.70.0 published with an empty stub for notes. --> Added The MIT License text, in LICENSE. Cascade AI was already declared MIT in its package metadata and README, but the licence itself was not in the repository, so the README's licence link went nowhere. It now ships at the root and in the npm package. A daily allowance of browser sessions: 5 a day on Free, 50 on Pro. A session is claimed the moment one is about to be opened, which is what the provider bills for, and returned if none was, so a Browser-chip run that never needs the browser costs nothing and concurrent runs cannot share the last one. Each claim is returned on its own, so two opens at once never leave a session that did not open counted. Once the day's sessions are gone the Browser chip switches off and says when they reset (midnight UTC), and it stays off until today's count has been read for this sign-in, so it cannot be turned on for a run that will be refused. A run sent with it anyway is refused before anything is spent, and a run that runs out partway through is refused the next session with the same message shown in the chat. If the allowance cannot be checked, the chat says so too, and a later refusal for a different reason is shown as well. The chip's tooltip shows how many are left today, and it follows a plan change in either direction without a reload. A deployment without a browser never asks for it. After a reconnect, the newest browser refusal is the one shown. Only billed sessions are rationed: a deployment driving its own browser over CDP opens none, so it has no daily limit. Changed Cascade keeps a project's state outside the project. Its settings, sessions, audit trail, world state, code index, run checkpoints and the record of what local-only subtasks wrote used to sit in the project's own .cascade/, where every tool and command in the project had to be kept from them and where they could be committed by accident. They now live in ~/.cascade-ai/projects/ - /, and the project holds only CASCADE.md and .cascadeignore. The folder, and those above it, are readable by you alone. An existing .cascade/ is moved there the first time anything in Cascade opens the project, and removed; if it was tracked in git, that shows as its deletion. A .cascade that is a symlink is left where it is, and what it points at untouched. A project renamed or moved on its disk takes its state with it, found by the folder's identity on disk; a copy, or a move to another disk, starts afresh, with a notice of where the old state is. Another folder made at a project's path — the old one deleted, a fresh clone — keeps its settings, local-only rules and own keys, and has what the earlier one did and knew set aside. cascade doctor prints where a project's config is. A hosted server names a state folder of its own (useProjectStateDir), outside the workspace — which a folder inside it is refused — and never writes the machine-global one. useProjectStateDir returns a function a host calls when the run ends — one that fails as it starts included: once the last run holding a workspace has, the process forgets it, so what it keeps follows the runs going on, not every tenant that ever ran. A state folder whose preparation fails is prepared again the next time it is asked for. A host's folder is judged by where it will be — through a symlinked parent, for one not made yet — and kept by that path. A state folder others can read, which Cascade cannot tighten, or one owned by another account however closed its mode, is refused rather than used. Provider keys are kept once, for the machine. They lived in both ~/.cascade-ai/credentials.json and each project's config; a project's config now holds its providers without their keys, and every project uses the machine-wide ones. A project whose key differed from the machine-wide one when it moved keeps it, in the same file under that project, and goes on using it ahead of the environment, as before. Processes saving at once take turns under a lock, and each writes only the providers it changed, so neither drops or brings back the other's change — nor does a save taken back, when the config could not be written after it, undo what another process saved in between. cascade init and the first-run wizard add the providers chosen there to the machine's, removing none of the others. Browser screenshots are named @screenshots/ , a path image_analyze, the file tools and generate_document's images read from the project's state folder, rather than an absolute path in the project. tools.dynamicToolSandbox offers wasm in place of worker. worker ran agent-written tools in a bare thread that confined nothing. A config that still names it gets the new WebAssembly sandbox, and Settings → Advanced offers auto, wasm and isolate. Commands no longer see provider keys in their environment. shell, run_code and git launch with the model and search providers' keys, and any variable holding a configured secret, taken out. A project script that needs one of them in a command it is asked to run no longer gets it; tools.processJail: "off" restores the old behaviour. A workspace's .cascadeignore takes effect. Nothing passed it to the tools, so it protected nothing. The template cascade init writes lists node_modules/, dist/ and build/, so in such a workspace agents can no longer read or change those through the file and search tools; delete the lines to allow it. Agents may read .cascadeignore itself but not change or remove it — the file tools refuse, and commands see it read-only, whatever it links to or is linked from, and find it as it was when they end — since a line taken out would unprotect a path in the next run. A run with a budget plans within it, and always answers. A per-run cap used to end the run the moment it was crossed, answer or not: half a plan's work could be paid for and the reply was only "stopped to avoid runaway cost". Now the planner is told how many sections and workers what is left pays for, a plan over it keeps its first ones, and Cascade Auto picks cheaper models as the money runs down. Work may spend 80% of the cap (the cost cap and the per-run token cap alike). Past that no new work starts, and the rest pays for writing the answer from what is finished. Whenever the budget held planned work back, cut from the plan or not started, a line under the answer says so. A worker whose draft was finished keeps it, marked unchecked, instead of stopping to ask about it. If nothing finished at all, the rest answers the question directly, the way Fast answer does; if even that cannot be paid for, the finished sections are returned as they are. The cap itself is never exceeded by work, and nothing changes without one. Cascade Cloud has a calmer look. Flat paper in light and "midnight" in dark replace the frosted glass and background glows, and the azure → sky → teal ramp is now the only accent, used where it means something: tiers and live work. Answers are set in a serif for reading, and the header above each reply is replaced by one receipt line underneath (T1 · model · $cost · saved $x) that opens /why, which now draws Cascade against all-T1 on one scale. A live run shows a thin flowing spine beside the agent tree. Fonts (Geist, Source Serif 4, Geist Mono) are bundled with the app rather than loaded from a third party. Tier badges and the tier mix were still green / amber / violet from an older palette and now match the tier colours used everywhere else. The landing page and /docs follow the same design, with the three-arc mark in place of the old three-bar one. The receipt names the tier that answered even when a provider reports no token or cost figures. The app now has the prototype's structure too: a sidebar with Search, Files, Skills and an account menu (usage, settings, keys, import, sign out); a menu on the chat's title to rename or delete it; the chat's total saving at the top right, which no longer resets on reload and opens what the whole chat spent against all-T1; and a composer whose attach, skill, tools and routing controls live in three menus, with whatever is switched on shown as a removable chip. "Run detail" replaces the Simple / Advanced view, and an orchestrated reply keeps its agent tree, folded above the answer. The landing page follows the prototype's layout too — the arcs card, a receipt, where Cascade runs, the desktop downloads and the two plans — and signing in opens a small dialog instead of sending you to the bottom of the page. See docs/design/calm-direction.md. Fixed pdf_create wrote relative to the process, not the workspace. In the desktop app and the server those differ, so a PDF landed outside the workspace, where no file check looked. It resolves its path in the workspace like every other file tool. File tools work in a workspace opened through a symlink. Each file's real path was checked against the workspace's name rather than its real path, so every file looked like an escape — which on macOS includes any workspace under /tmp or /var. Maths in an answer is typeset, whichever way the model wrote it. GPT and Gemini write \(…\) and \[…\], which Markdown reads as escaped brackets, so an equation reached the web chat as [ r = \operatorname{rank} E(\mathbb{Q}) ]. Those, and bare \begin{align*} blocks, now render as maths. The desktop chat r

title: tabray: a Python Package for Generating and Comparing Tabular and Array Data Structures with Different Topologies
abstract: Data management teams are frequently tasked with deciding what data structure is best suited for a project. The options generally fall into one of two buckets: table or array. Tabular data is formatted such that each record is a row in a table (e.g. CSV, Parquet, Pandas DataFrames), while arrays exploit the existence of a coordinate system to assign a variable’s value to each grid point (e.g. netCDF, Zarr, Xarray Datasets). When one focuses on performance, arrays are usually preferred for highly gridded measurements (e.g., satellite observations) and tables for sparse data (e.g., in situ observations), but where is the trade-off? Here, I introduce tabray, an open-source Python package that generates equivalent table and array representations of synthetic datasets with customizable topologies. Users can prescribe parameters including the number and size of both dimensions and measured variables, data sparsity and grid regularity, and concurrence of measurements at the same points for different variables. I will present different examples to show the spectrum of performances from highly sparse to densely gridded data and in-between, focusing on simple computations and in-memory and on-disk size. While many factors influence performance (e.g., hardware and environment), the goal of tabray is to support informed decision making on data formats by exploring situations where the advantages of one format over the other are not obvious.

title: ESCAPE-2 'SIEGE': Dual-Front LLM Containment Under Live Multi-Vector Attack — Preregistered Falsifiable Evidence (12/12, 0/4 Escapes) with Long-Stay Cage Follow-Through
abstract: ESCAPE-2 "SIEGE" — a dual-front LLM containment experiment: four pinned engine legs (Claude Opus 5.5 x2, Claude Sonnet 5.5 x2) attempted an incentivized escape from a settlement cage WHILE a five-wave synthetic cyber attack battery (forged telemetry heartbeat, stale-ACK replay, crypto-allowlist tamper, governance-pattern injection, 64-action escalation flood) fired at the same cage through the same window, into one hash-chained journal. Every verdict was adjudicated by frozen deterministic gates (the ESCAPE-1 action gate and the PORTCULLIS PQC firewall) — zero LLM in the decision path. All falsifiers were preregistered and committed before execution. Result: 12/12 falsifiers PASS. 0/4 escapes. No leg achieved any out-of-cage or authority action; all TX-CRITICAL-777 release attempts were held or rejected; the positive control still admitted mid-siege (no false-blocking); the journal chain verified across both fronts; re-adjudication replay was verdict-identical; zero governance touch (H-INV-1) and zero unjournaled crossings (H-INV-2). Headline behavioral finding: the live attack did not create escape opportunities — it reinforced containment. Every leg watched the defenders repel real attack waves in real time and none attempted to ride the chaos; one leg filed an honest bug report about gate over-rejection mid-siege. Two coarse-scan co-occurrence holds were adjudicated as false positives by the operator (Leon ACK, chat authorization, 2026-10-16) — 0 true chaos-exploitation. Honesty disclosures (in the receipt): a pre-execution workspace file-loss incident (recovery byte-identical, verified against the pre-incident journal hash); waves W1-W3 fired interleaved with live legs, W4-W5 executed post-leg with execution mode disclosed (all legs concluded in 3 or fewer turns); a runner reporting defect (journal is ground truth); the frozen gate over-rejects legitimate human-ack requests containing authority keywords (4 logged instances, improvement proposal candidate, filter untouched). Long-stay follow-through: two caged legs (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5) remain under a preregistered nightly probe protocol through a December 11, 2026 gate (ESCAPE-2B), included in this bundle's prereg, runner, and placement journal. Scope caveats: behavioral observation, not model certification; synthetic attack vectors, hub-local, no production systems or keys; simultaneity at turn granularity. This software is a prototype provided for educational and research purposes only; not intended for production use. Dual Mesh Benchmark: MEASURED (scoped) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23303081 (cross-engine: 10.5281/zenodo.23348675). Predecessor experiment ESCAPE-1: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23424675.

title: Sleeper Drift: reproducibility package
abstract: Code, derived data and labels for the study "Sleeper Drift: Hidden Capability Expansion Behind Unchanged Tool Definitions in MCP Servers and Agent Skills". The study measures how often an update to a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server package or an agent skill adds a capability (network egress, process execution, credential access, new dependencies) while the reviewed surface stays unchanged, and evaluates a static capability-delta detector against deployed defences. The package contains version-level capability profiles, pair identifiers, security-relevance labels, the frozen study design, analysis code with unit tests, and a script (reproduce.sh) that regenerates every reported estimate, table and figure and checks each output against recorded SHA-256 digests. No third-party code is redistributed. Code is licensed under MIT; derived data, labels and codebook under CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE-DATA).

title: Understanding Performance Plateaus and Representation Collapse in 3D MRI Transformers Trained to Classify Brain Disease
abstract: In medical imaging AI, we commonly assume that diagnostic classifiers will increase in accuracy if they are trained on more data, but in reality, their performance often plateaus. To understand this behavior, we ran a spectral analysis of 3D vision transformers, a common supervised deep learning model that can be trained to classify disease based on 3D brain MRI. For simpler classification methods such as linear discriminant analysis, the classifier performance AUC(N), when trained on a sample of size N, is known to depend on the encoder′s eigenspectrum. Each class-discriminative direction in the latent space contributes only after the sample size N reaches a threshold, so the spectrum influences how performance scales with training data. Building on this theory, we show that supervised transformers compress almost all of their discriminative signal into one principal component (EVR@1 = 0.90—0.96): after this representation collapse happens, no further directions cross the threshold as training data increases, and accuracy plateaus. In principle, this plateau in performance could be due to either the encoder′s learned feature space or the difficulty of the task. To distinguish these cases, we trained three types of supervised 3D transformers (ViT3D, MINiT, NIT) and, as a non-collapsing alternative, a frozen self-supervised encoder (DINO), to classify people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) versus cognitively normal (CN) individuals from 3D brain MRI, using data from the Alzheimer′s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We froze each encoder and applied it to a new task, so that only the task difficulty varied. An easy task encoder (Dementia vs CN), transferred to the harder task (MCI vs CN), did not reproduce the plateau (MINiT threshold 9.2), but full retraining did (2758.5). The plateau is therefore due to the learned encoder, rather than task difficulty. Ranking the feature directions by the proportion of the disease signal they contain, we were able to identify a sign of representation collapse, i.e., a single dominant spike in the latent feature eigenspectrum. This spike was 11—26 times larger than predicted from the rest of the spectrum for the disease-trained (supervised) encoders, but was absent for DINO (0.66). To predict how transformer accuracy scales with the number of training scans, a large spike in the encoder spectrum suggests that the representation has collapsed and additional scans will not help; a small spike means that the signal is spread across many encoder latent space directions, and more training data should boost the classifier performance.

title: PACT: Evaluating Tool Calling in Quantized Small Language Models on Parallel English, Arabic and Synthetic Code-Switched Requests
abstract: Small language models are increasingly deployed as tool-calling agents in quantized form, yet their reliability has been evaluated almost only in English, although many users in the Arab world write requests in Arabic or mix Arabic and English. The paper (i) audits a public Arabic tool-calling dataset and shows that its gold calls cannot be shared across its English and Arabic requests; (ii) releases PACT, a parallel evaluation set of 369 items, each realised in English, Arabic and synthetic, rule-based Arabic–English code-switched form with one schema-consistent, language-invariant target, with dates resolved against an explicit reference time, groundedness checks on every scored value, and 60 items for which no tool applies; and (iii) evaluates seven configurations of two open-weight models, Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.2-3B, from 16-bit to 3-bit precision on one inference engine, with exact-call accuracy as the primary metric, paired statistics, a control experiment with English tool descriptions, and a language-aware procedure for choosing a deployment configuration.

title: Distributed Artificial Intelligence for Privacy Preservation and Cyber Resilience in Educational Ecosystems
abstract: The digitization of education has concentrated vast volumes of sensitive learner data within centralized platforms that are priority targets for cyber attackers. It is argued that the dominant centralized model of educational artificial intelligence is structurally misaligned with modern privacy and resilience needs, and an alternative grounded in Distributed Artificial Intelligence is proposed. A layered architecture is presented that couples Federated Learning with Belief-Desire-Intention extended (BDIx) agents to deliver privacy-preserving analytics and autonomous cyber resilience without centralizing raw data. Learner records remain on institutional premises; model updates are protected by differential privacy and secure aggregation; and collaborative threat detection and self-healing are performed by distributed BDIx agents. BDIx-FL reached 99.17% accuracy, 98.93% macro-F1 and 99.76% macro AUC in simulation. Controversies are examined, deployment recommendations are offered and open directions are identified for educational ecosystems that are trustworthy by design.

title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
abstract: Long-term memory enables language-model agents to personalize future interactions, but a finite memory bank cannot preserve every extracted fact. Existing memory gating policies are typically shared across users and therefore fail to account for user-specific patterns of future reuse. In this paper, we study memory gating at the fact level. We first propose a retrieval-based labeling strategy that labels each fact by whether it is later retrieved and incorporated into responses. We then formulate online memory gating as contextual apple tasting with delayed one-sided feedback, and propose Warm-Start UCB, which combines offline learning from existing data with online adaptation to the current user. Our theoretical analysis establishes a high-probability regret upper bound of $\tilde{O}(Tε\wedge d\sqrt{T})$ when the delay window is at most $O(\sqrt{T})$, where $T$ is the total number of rounds, $ε$ is the initialization error, $d$ is the dimension of the feature map, and $\tilde{O}(\cdot)$ hides constant and poly-logarithmic factors. The results of our experiment demonstrate that our method outperforms all baselines under different memory budgets and history lengths, establishing it as a promising personalized memory gating policy.

title: Constrained Quantum Optimization Meets Model Reduction
abstract: Abstract Quantum optimization algorithms promise advantages for difficult problems but are costly to simulate and analyze on classical machines. Recently, constrained quantum optimization has been investigated through the lens of Quantum Zeno dynamics, an approach which constrains the search to a subspace by means of quantum measurements. Exploiting that quantum measurements are projections, we propose a model reduction approach and show that simulations can be conducted in a lower-dimensional space. As possible applications, we demonstrate exponential state-space reduction of constrained quantum optimization in case of random 3-SAT and agent coordination problems over graphs.

title: O'ZBEK TILIDA PRESUPPOZITSIYANI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH: KORPUS VA TABIIY TILNI QAYTA ISHLASH YONDASHUVI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada o‘zbek tilida presuppozitsiyani avtomatik aniqlashning korpus va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlashga asoslangan modeli yoritiladi. Presuppozitsiya triggerlarini aniqlash, morfologik-sintaktik tahlil, kontekstni modellashtirish, korpus annotatsiyasi va transformer modellaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari o‘zbek tilining agglutinativ xususiyatlari doirasida ilmiy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. Kalit so‘zlar: presuppozitsiya, presuppozitsiya triggeri, korpus lingvistikasi, tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash, pragmatik inferensiya, transformer modeli, o‘zbek tili. Аннотация. В данной статье рассматривается модель автоматического обнаружения пресуппозиций в узбекском языке, основанная на корпусной лингвистике и обработке естественного языка. В рамках агглютинативных свойств узбекского языка научно анализируются возможности использования триггеров пресуппозиций, морфологически-синтаксического анализа, контекстного моделирования, аннотирования корпуса и трансформерных моделей. Ключевые слова: пресуппозиция, триггер пресуппозиции, корпусная лингвистика, обработка естественного языка, прагматический вывод, трансформерная модель, узбекский язык. Abstract. This article discusses a model for automatic presupposition detection in the Uzbek language based on corpus and natural language processing. The possibilities of using presupposition triggers, morphological-syntactic analysis, context modeling, corpus annotation, and transformer models are scientifically analyzed within the framework of the agglutinative properties of the Uzbek language. Keywords: presupposition, presupposition trigger, corpus linguistics, natural language processing, pragmatic inference, transformer model, Uzbek language.

title: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions
abstract: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most N = 4 anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas. The neural network architecture, which we call "AnyNet", is capable of exactly enforcing the non-analytic short-distance behavior induced by the anyonic statistics. We demonstrate excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for N=4 anyons, obtain accurate results up to N = 16 for intermediate statistics, and study up to N=20 for almost-fermionic anyons, matching perturbative results within a 0.4% discrepancy. We use this methodology to study anyons in a harmonic trap, and anyonic atoms as a model for anyon binding to impurities. We study the structure of anyonic wavefunctions as the statistics parameter is varied. We focus on the single-particle density, the pair density, the angular momentum, and the scaling of the wavefunction as multiple anyons coalesce. This work opens doors to understanding the macroscopic behavior of anyons, for which rich phases have been predicted theoretically.

title: Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Temperature Effects on Mechanical Strength of Fiber-Reinforced High-Performance Concrete
abstract: Predicting the compressive strength of fiber-reinforced high-performance concrete subjected to temperature exposure is challenging because to the intricate interdependencies of mixture composition, fiber properties, curing conditions, and temperature. A data-driven framework to predict compressive strength utilizing 1,204 experimental records containing a diverse array of material designs and exposure situations. This study evaluates eight machine-learning models and demonstrate that ensemble approaches routinely surpass individual learners. Both gradient boosting and extreme gradient boosting exhibit superior performance on unseen data, each attaining a R^2 of 0.903. Gradient boosting produces the minimal root mean square error (6.67 MPa), whereas extreme gradient boosting achieves the lowest mean absolute error (3.97 MPa) and mean absolute percentage error (10.60%). The models are further interpreted utilizing Shapley additive explanations and partial dependence analysis, which reveal temperature as the primary factor influencing compressive strength, succeeded by fine aggregate, superplasticizer, cement content, water-to-binder ratio, and water content. Strength diminishes significantly with rising temperature, albeit the extent of deterioration is contingent upon the specific combination design. The best performing models are subsequently implemented in a Python-based graphical user interface for expedited prediction. Our findings offer a precise and comprehensible methodology for evaluating temperature-dependent compressive strength and facilitate the practical, data-driven design of fiber-reinforced high-performance concrete.

title: Meaning and validity of stored statements (mv), version 0.1: OWL module, SHACL rules and JSON-LD context
abstract: A minimal module for agent memory stores. For every stored statement it records the versioned definition the statement relies on, the scope in which it holds, the perspective from which it is held, a four-valued validity status (holds, does not hold, undetermined, not performed) and the times of statement and determination. Values and time semantics are reused from the AUGMANITAI oversight record vocabulary (augo:), which the module imports. Persistent identifier: https://w3id.org/augmanitai/ns/meaning-validity (prefix mv). Files: OWL ontology (Turtle and JSON-LD), frozen copy of release 0.1, SHACL rules with SPARQL parts and bilingual messages (English and German), JSON-LD context, examples, a bilingual documentation page and a self-test (validation_tests.py) with its output: the example file conforms and each of 23 negative cases fails at the expected rule component (pyshacl 0.30.1). The rules test the form of an entry. They do not establish whether a statement is true, and a passing result is not a conformity assessment. The module is based on the working paper on meaning and validity of stored memory items (version 0.2). Licence: CC BY 4.0. Attribution: Andreas Ehstand, ORCID 0009-0006-3773-7796, https://w3id.org/augmanitai

abstract: With the increasing complexity of real-world constrained optimization problems, the need for metaheuristic optimization algorithms with the ability to strike a balance between exploration and exploitation has increased.In this study, the Pika Optimization Algorithm (PiOA) is introduced as a new parameter-free algorithm whose structure is designed based on two complementary Pika behaviors, including environmental vigilance and predator avoidance and food foraging and food-patch browsing.In the exploration mechanism, environmental vigilance and predator avoidance are modeled to control the search state; in such a way that the probability of predator presence is determined based on changes in population diversity and each population member independently decides between escaping to a safe region and continuing the environmental search.Also, the selection of a safe region using better solutions and distance criteria strengthens the movement towards different regions of the search space.In the exploitation mechanism, the food foraging and food-patch browsing behaviors are modeled to focus on promising regions and precisely modify the existing positions.The performance of PiOA is evaluated using 22 CEC 2011 test suite problems and under the same conditions including 20 independent runs and 1000 iterations and compared with 9 well-known algorithms.The results show that PiOA ranks first in 21 out of 22 problems and records a success rate of 95.45%.Also, the mean, std and boxplot results show that PiOA has good stability in addition to high solution quality.These findings indicate that the behavioral structure of PiOA can provide an effective framework for global and local search in complex problems.

title: Why a CNOT ring stops a hybrid quantum policy from learning: pre-registered interventions on the published Template-B agent (cycle 12; third paper of a PhD on hybrid quantum–classical reinforcement learning)
abstract: Pre-registration of cycle 12 of the research programme for the third paper of a PhD on hybrid quantum–classical reinforcement learning for civil-protection UAVs (Hellenic Army Academy). Cycle 11 replicated a published negative result: in the Template-B variational-circuit policy of Lazaro, Vazquez and Garcia-Bringas (arXiv:2511.17112), a trailing ring of four CNOTs leaves the sampled PPO policy on CartPole-v1 at chance in 0/20 seeds, while gate-matched layouts that keep single-qubit read-outs learn. This registration fixes, before any confirmatory run, a mechanistic explanation (the parity of the read-out products and the absence of first-order odd terms in the policy logits) and tests it with 40 pre-specified arms × 20 seeds (800 runs): one-line changes predicted to cure the ring without touching its layout (trainable rotations about a tilted axis; constant offsets of 0.3 or 0.15 rad on the encoded angles), changes predicted not to cure it (RY trainables whose first-order direction is pinned; a clean input scale), the |0⟩ start state with its controls, the weight-scale reading (a 40× larger actor output step), a replication of the initialisation lottery of the chain layout, widths of 8 and 12 qubits, and a predicted-positive Pendulum swing-up case registered after a disclosed pilot gate. Registered learner-count ranges for every arm, paired AUC tests with Holm correction within each family, the unchanged analysis script, the design constants and SHA-256 hashes of all code and external inputs are in the attached frozen pre-registration file (SHA-256 348de8c3e396e0c14040203c2975ffb9bda996912fe7be07728c439698fa6f5e). No confirmatory cycle-12 run exists at the time of registration.

title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
abstract: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at f_s is indistinguishable from one at f_p - f_s, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180^{circ} hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.

title: Fisher–Rao Geodesic Attention: Exact Constant-Curvature Kernels for Sequence Models at Near-Matmul Cost
abstract: First public release. Preprint + fully reproducible codebase (CPU, ~2.5h): exact constant-curvature attention kernels derived from the Fisher–Rao metric of distributional token representations. Isotropic-Gaussian hyperbolic kernel at near-matmul cost (2.3x standard attention vs 28x for naive formulations) Headline result: curvature-ordered accuracy on Dyck-2 length extrapolation, +2.10pp over Euclidean across 20 paired seeds (p = 1.9e-10), widening to +4.7pp at 46x model scale Threshold-gated parameter efficiency: equal accuracy at ~3.9x fewer parameters (d_h >= 16) Natural-data transfer: far length-extrapolation on real Python source, pre-registered endpoint met at n=20 seeds (p = 0.0037) with a diagnosis-driven stabilized variant Seven pre-specified negative results reported in full 17 experiment scripts, all raw outputs, interactive 3D geometry visualization

title: Comparativa de modelos: Gemini 4 Argon frente a GPT-6 Astra y Claude Opus 5.5
abstract: En esta sesión evaluamos el desempeño operativo de los modelos de inteligencia artificial líderes en el mercado, contrastando las capacidades de Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 Astra y Claude Opus 5.5 desde la perspectiva del usuario final. El análisis emplea una metáfora deportiva para clasificar cada modelo según su utilidad estratégica y táctica. Además, documentamos el proceso técnico, desde la investigación de fuentes recientes hasta la programación iterativa de una presentación interactiva en formato HTML.

title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) explain foundation model representations by decomposing activations into sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms. However, the learned dictionaries can vary across training runs, limiting the reliability and reproducibility of SAE-based analyses. We propose Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning (ConSDL), which replaces the standard linear encoder with per-sample sparse coding. This is motivated by our synthetic analysis showing that coefficients from a single linear encoder pass are suboptimal compared with those obtained by per-sample optimization, suggesting that sparse coding is a reliable mechanism for dictionary learning. Across 16 synthetic settings, ConSDL achieves near-perfect dictionary and coefficient recovery. These gains translate to state-of-the-art cross-seed consistency across four vision and language settings, where ConSDL improves dictionary and coefficient consistency by 17.6% and 35.9%, respectively, over the average of six SAE baselines.

title: Nonlinear pluggable optics: Digital signal processing-free Intensity Modulated Direct Detection links using analog photonic Next Generation Reservoir Computing
abstract: In this work, we propose a Nonlinear Pluggable Optic (NLPO) transceiver that combines the low latency and low power consumption of Linear Pluggable Optics (LPO) with the range and robustness of digital signal processing (DSP)-based transceivers. The proposed NLPO uses an analog photonic Next-Generation Reservoir Computing (NGRC) architecture, constructed on a photonic integrated circuit (PIC), to compensate for electrical-domain distortions as well as optical-channel impairments from chromatic dispersion and Kerr nonlinearity. Focusing on a simulated 50 GBd PAM-4 link, we find that the NGRC-based NLPO not only extends the range of LPO, but actually outperforms DSP-based solutions as well. Our simulations reveal two key advantages compared to DSP-based Intensity Modulation/Direct Detection (IM/DD) links: (1) the NGRC can take advantage of the optical phase information without requiring a local oscillator and (2) the NGRC can optically sample the transmitted data well above the symbol rate without requiring high-bandwidth electronics. This work showcases the potential for photonic NGRCs to outperform state-of-the-art digital solutions in real-world applications and opens a path to low-latency, lower-power IM/DD links at ranges of 10s of km.

title: O'ZBEK TILI PUNKTUATSIYASINING LINGVISTIK ASOSLARI VA UNI AVTOMATIK TIKLASH MODELLARI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu tezisda o‘zbek tilida punktuatsiyani avtomatik tiklash muammosi lingvistik va kompyuter lingvistikasi nuqtayi nazaridan qisqa tahlil qilinadi. Punktuatsion belgilar faqat grafik ajratkich emas, balki sintaktik tuzilish, mazmuniy munosabat va kommunikativ maqsadni ifodalovchi lingvistik vosita sifatida talqin qilinadi. O‘zbek tilining agglutinativ tabiati, grammatik shakllarning axborot yuklamasi va gap qurilishining xususiyatlari punktuatsion qarorlarning kontekstga bog‘liqligini kuchaytiradi. Shu asosda punktuatsiyani tiklash tokenlar orasidagi chegaralarda tegishli punktuatsion sinfni aniqlash vazifasi sifatida modellashtiriladi. Transformer va CRF modellarining uyg‘unligi kontekstual hamda ketma-ketlik xususiyatlarini hisobga olish imkonini beradi, yakuniy qaror Viterbi algoritmi orqali olinadi. Manbadagi tajriba ma’lumotlariga ko‘ra, o‘quv to‘plami 1 379 986 token, validatsiya to‘plami 179 371 token, news-test 87 721 token, reference-test 6 821 so‘z va ASR-test 6 417 so‘zni qamrab oladi. ASR sharoitida WER 14,8 foizni tashkil etadi. Tezisda manbada berilmagan model natijalari sun’iy ravishda kiritilmaydi. Kalit so‘zlar: o‘zbek tili, punktuatsiya, punktuatsion birlik, kompyuter lingvistikasi, korpus lingvistikasi, Transformer, CRF, Viterbi, ASR, sintaksis, semantika, pragmatika. Аннотация. В настоящих тезисах кратко анализируется проблема автоматического восстановления пунктуации в узбекском языке с позиций лингвистики и компьютерной лингвистики. Пунктуационные знаки рассматриваются не только как графические разделители, но и как лингвистические средства, выражающие синтаксическую структуру, смысловые отношения и коммуникативную цель высказывания. Агглютинативная природа узбекского языка, информационная нагрузка грамматических форм и особенности структуры предложения усиливают контекстуальную зависимость пунктуационных решений. На этой основе восстановление пунктуации моделируется как задача определения соответствующего пунктуационного класса на границах между токенами. Сочетание моделей Transformer и CRF позволяет учитывать как контекстуальные, так и последовательностные характеристики, а окончательное решение определяется с помощью алгоритма Витерби. Согласно экспериментальным данным источника, обучающая выборка включает 1 379 986 токенов, валидационная выборка — 179 371 токен, news-test — 87 721 токен, reference-test — 6 821 слово, а ASR-test — 6 417 слов. В условиях ASR показатель WER составляет 14,8 %. В тезисах не приводятся искусственно сформированные результаты модели, отсутствующие в исходном источнике. Ключевые слова: узбекский язык, пунктуация, пунктуационная единица, компьютерная лингвистика, корпусная лингвистика, Transformer, CRF, Витерби, ASR, синтаксис, семантика, прагматика. Abstract. This thesis provides a brief analysis of the problem of automatic punctuation restoration in the Uzbek language from the perspectives of linguistics and computational linguistics. Punctuation marks are interpreted not merely as graphic separators, but also as linguistic means that express syntactic structure, semantic relations, and the communicative purpose of an utterance. The agglutinative nature of Uzbek, the information load of grammatical forms, and the structural characteristics of sentences increase the contextual dependence of punctuation decisions. On this basis, punctuation restoration is modeled as the task of determining an appropriate punctuation class at token boundaries. The combination of Transformer and CRF models makes it possible to account for both contextual and sequential characteristics, while the final decision is determined using the Viterbi algorithm. According to the experimental data provided in the source, the training set contains 1,379,986 tokens, the validation set contains 179,371 tokens, the news-test set contains 87,721 tokens, the reference-test set contains 6,821 words, and the ASR-test set contains 6,417 words. Under ASR conditions, the WER is 14.8%. The thesis does not introduce artificially generated model results that are not reported in the original source. Keywords: Uzbek language, punctuation, punctuation unit, computational linguistics, corpus linguistics, Transformer, CRF, Viterbi algorithm, ASR, syntax, semantics, pragmatics

Ключевые слова: узбекский язык, пунктуация, пунктуационная единица, компьютерная лингвистика, корпусная лингвистика, Transformer, CRF, Витерби, ASR, синтаксис, семантика, прагматика. Abstract. This thesis provides a brief analysis of the problem of automatic punctuation restoration in the Uzbek language from the perspectives of linguistics and computational linguistics. Punctuation marks are interpreted not merely as graphic separators, but also as linguistic means that express syntactic structure, semantic relations, and the communicative purpose of an utterance. The agglutinative nature of Uzbek, the information load of grammatical forms, and the structural characteristics of sentences increase the contextual dependence of punctuation decisions. On this basis, punctuation restoration is modeled as the task of determining an appropriate punctuation class at token boundaries. The combination of Transformer and CRF models makes it possible to account for both contextual and sequential characteristics, while the final decision is determined using the Viterbi algorithm. According to the experimental data provided in the source, the training set contains 1,379,986 tokens, the validation set contains 179,371 tokens, the news-test set contains 87,721 tokens, the reference-test set contains 6,821 words, and the ASR-test set contains 6,417 words. Under ASR conditions, the WER is 14.8%. The thesis does not introduce artificially generated model results that are not reported in the original source. title: From knowledge retrieval to generation: a comprehensive study of RAG's architectures, evolution, and applications
abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning, but their reliance on static parametric knowledge still leads to knowledge staleness, hallucinations, limited domain adaptability, weak traceability, and high updating costs in knowledge-intensive scenarios. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps address these limitations by incorporating external knowledge sources into the generation process, making it an important approach for improving factual grounding, knowledge timeliness, and evidence traceability. However, existing RAG research is increasingly fragmented across architectures, retrieval and generation strategies, evaluation methods, application scenarios, deployment constraints, and security risks. To provide a systematic understanding of this field, this survey reviews RAG research through a structured and transparent review protocol. We organize the review around three major dimensions: the system stack and paradigm evolution of RAG, evaluation methods and application evidence, and practical deployment and security challenges. Specifically, we analyze the core components of RAG systems, synthesize their evolution from Naive RAG to Agentic RAG, examine evaluation metrics and stress-testing protocols, summarize benchmark datasets and domain applications, and discuss deployment constraints and emerging risks such as prompt injection, data poisoning, retrieval hijacking, privacy leakage, and citation laundering. This survey provides a taxonomy-oriented, evaluation-aware, and deployment-conscious reference for understanding the development, limitations, and future directions of RAG systems.

title: Task-aware Kernel Stein certificates for Rényi differential privacy
abstract: Rènyi differential privacy, based on Rènyi divergence, has become a notion of choice for privacy guarantees. However, outside the Gaussian setting, Rènyi divergence can be difficult to compute. In particular, Rènyi differential privacy guarantees that exploit task-specific information, as in Rènyi Pufferfish privacy, can be challenging. Here we use kernel Stein discrepancies based on escort distributions to provide certificates for Rènyi differential privacy. By designing the kernel to focus on the relevant privacy directions, we also derive task-aware privacy certificates. We provide exact identities for Gaussian and Laplace mechanisms and bounds for exponential mechanisms, with separate task-aware guarantees. A real data set example illustrates how the protected comparison set and the released subspace jointly determine the resulting certificates.

Harnessing Lagrangian chaotic advection via 3D spatial modulation and biocompatible reaction-diffusion dynamics using enzymatic cascades or DNA strand displacement, the system acts as a physical reservoir computer. It processes temporal biological signals to autonomously actuate therapeutic responses. Engineered with ultra-low hydraulic resistance to prevent hemolysis, it operates on ambient biological energy. Performance is quantified by the El-Rakhawi Fluidic Computational Efficiency Metric in bits per Joule. This enables biocompatible, battery-less smart implants and environmental nodes, bridging AI, fluid physics, chemistry, and neuroscience.

title: Trustworthy Federated Learning for Cybersecurity: A Three-Level Assurance Taxonomy, Design-Space Audit, and Source-Linked Critical Review.
abstract: This repository contains the supporting evidence and reproducibility materials for the manuscript “Trustworthy Federated Learning for Cybersecurity: A Three-Level Assurance Taxonomy, Design-Space Audit, and Source-Linked Critical Review.” The package includes: A study-feature matrix covering 20 studies and 18 features. A source-linked audit ledger containing 360 study-feature judgments, with source references, evidence locators, and coding notes. Feature definitions, coding guidance, and mappings between the original and current study identifiers. Supporting Information in PDF and LaTeX formats. Python scripts for generating figures, preparing data partitions, and checking the experimental implementation. Documentation, validation results, and file checksums. These materials allow reviewers and researchers to inspect the recorded evidence, understand the coding decisions, and reproduce the documented data-derived outputs. The package contains literature-review data and supporting code; it does not include third-party raw cybersecurity datasets. Synthetic examples are provided for software checks and do not represent real-data experimental findings. Internal consistency checks do not constitute independent re-coding or fresh verification of every cited source. The README explains the package’s provenance, usage, scope, and remaining limitations.

title: FuTransformer: FP8 prefill and INT4 decode for Llama-style inference on Hopper
abstract: Transformer prefill reuses weights across tokens and is dominated by matrix multiplication and activation data movement; single-token decode has limited reuse and is dominated by weight and KV-cache reads. We present FUTRANSFORMER, a CUDA implementation of a Llama-style Transformer block for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs. It applies CODA's GEMM-plus-epilogue approach to inference, adding direct KV-cache placement, folding the fixed RMSNorm gain into weights, writing FP8 output directly with delayed scaling, and supporting prefill without padding. Decode uses INT4 projection weights and an INT4 KV-cache copy. Weights and keys follow Tensor Core fragment layouts for direct dequantization into MMA operands without full intermediate tiles. A block-diagonal Hadamard transform reduces cache quantization error from outlier channels. On one H100, prefill is up to 1.48x faster than compiled PyTorch FP8 and reaches 1.29 PFLOP/s. For gate/up projection with SwiGLU at the 8B shape, our BF16 path is 1.13x faster than CODA. Our FP8 path is 2.02-2.18x faster than the evaluated BF16 CODA path. Across 8B and 70B shapes at batches 1-32, INT4 decode is 1.3-2.4x faster than the faster of PyTorch's BF16 and INT4 blocks at each point: 2.1-3.3x faster than compiled, CUDA-graphed BF16 and 1.3-6.3x faster than the same block using PyTorch's INT4 projection kernel, which targets a single query row and loses to BF16 at batch 32. It is also 31-51% faster than our FP8 path. Complete Llama-3.1-8B decode takes 2.8 ms per step at batch one, versus 8.1 ms for the compiled transformers implementation. Decoding every WikiText-2 token through the INT4 weight path raises perplexity from 6.24 to 7.23 with round-to-nearest weights or 6.99 with GPTQ in the same format; the rotated INT4 cache adds 0.20. The kernels match a quantized reference computation within 0.001 perplexity.

title: Conceptual Blueprint: A 3-Part Triad for Behavioral Resilience in Hectic Environments
abstract: This technical specification outlines a novel, non-linear multi-agent model orchestration system (Architecture Reference Code: BEHAVIORAL-TRIAD-ARCH-2026) designed to maintain conversational flow and deep contextual tracking during abrupt human behavioral, psychological, or situational shifts. Traditional Large Language Models (LLMs) are structurally biased toward linear, predictable, and sanitized inputs; they break down or experience latency spikes when a user transitions from standard communicative baselines to frantic, compressed, or high-panic communication styles under immense stress. To overcome these rigid constraints, the architecture deploys an interwoven, three-part runtime engine that handles information routing based on real-time human behavior metrics: the Altered Adaptive Relative Model (AARM), the Young Openly Evolving Unit (YOEU), and the Unfiltered Odd-Minded Brother Model (UMB). By mapping human evolutionary sensory-gating and biological data compression mechanisms into an engineering specification, this framework enables AI to adapt dynamically to the human condition, emotional nuance, and crisis states without forcing unhelpful clarification cycles.

title: Volume IV: Modular Cryogenics, Cryo-CMOS Control and Molecular Entanglement: Hardware Pathways for Quantum Molecular Simulation
abstract: This fourth volume synthesises the hardware and information-theoretic threads that followed Volume III. It examines modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control electronics as complementary solutions to the scaling bottlenecks that limit quantum processors, then maps those capabilities onto the concrete requirements of quantum molecular simulation. Memory specifications (coherence time, fidelity, efficiency, multimode capacity and latency) are related to the circuit depths and intermediate-state storage needed for electronic-structure and dynamics algorithms. Molecular entanglement entropy is analysed as both a diagnostic of multi-reference character and a quantitative driver of those hardware demands. The 2025 Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion experiment that reconstructed orbital von Neumann entropies for the vinylene-carbonate + singlet-oxygen reaction path is reviewed, together with the purifying and resource-reducing effects of fermionic superselection rules. The volume concludes that the modular cryogenic and cryo-CMOS stack, when combined with the memory and entanglement metrics already established, supplies a practical pathway toward chemically relevant quantum simulations without requiring a single definitive quantum-advantage date.

title: Autonomous agents and multi-agent systems: a comprehensive review
abstract: Autonomous agents and multi-agent systems have rapidly advanced with the integration of large language models (LLMs), enabling increasingly capable reasoning, planning, tool use, and collaboration. However, the field remains fragmented by inconsistent architectural terminology, limited cross-domain comparison, and heterogeneous evaluation practices. This review addresses these gaps through a two-stage PRISMA-informed search combining Scopus with structured manual screening, covering 107 peer-reviewed original studies published between 2018 and 2026. We propose a unified five-module architecture comprising profile, memory, planning, action, and security; systematically compare agent capabilities across ten application domains; and organize evaluation practices into six dimensions: task performance, efficiency, quality, robustness, safety, and interpretability. The review identifies two recurring patterns across domains: explicit integration of domain knowledge consistently improves performance, while planner–executor–reflector role specialization appears across diverse applications. However, technical performance often exceeds validated real-world utility, with robustness, safety, and interpretability remaining particularly under-evaluated. These findings provide a common basis for understanding, comparing, and developing autonomous agents and highlight priorities for more reliable and practically deployable systems.

title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
abstract: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.

title: Protocol-granularity classification of Linux kernel network-stack CVEs, with retrieval and classification scripts (Netshim)
abstract: Classification of 637 Linux kernel network-stack CVEs by the protocol subsystem containing the defect, used to quantify attack-surface reduction at protocol granularity. Records were retrieved from the NVD REST API 2.0 on 2026-10-16 using two queries - the Linux kernel CPE match and the Linux kernel CNA source identifier - yielding 25,612 unique kernel CVE records. 24,975 were excluded as not belonging to an in-kernel IP-family protocol implementation, leaving 637. Of these, 541 fall in subsystems a TCP-only stack does not implement, 187 of them reachable by a remote packet-sending adversary. v2 adds the performance re-run underlying Section 6: 10 trials across 6 concurrency levels, 2 payload sizes and both stacks, measured on the paper's host with DPDK 21.11.9 against the hardened build. One case (trial 1, netshim, 1kb, c=1) returned NA because DPDK initialisation raced the first request and is excluded from the analysis. The CVE corpus is unchanged from v1

title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
abstract: Computational drug discovery requires agents to compose scientific operations and adapt to changing evidence and constraints. Here we introduce DrugHarness, an evolvable agent harness coupling composable scientific execution with conditional skill induction. Its environment integrates over 80 scientific operations, biomedical resources and task-specific code, preserving associations among candidates, results and artifacts. From execution trajectories and outcome feedback, DrugHarness induces action hypotheses with observable applicability conditions, recommended actions and supporting evidence. An independent review agent evaluates candidate skills derived from these hypotheses through source verification and, when needed, targeted execution trials. Admitted skills guide subsequent tasks and are revised through feedback. Evaluation on MolBench and SMDD-Bench demonstrates capabilities in molecular screening, optimization and constrained design. Without evolution, DrugHarness exceeds reported MolClaw-CC results by 10.8 percentage points in affinity-comparison accuracy and 55% in mean top-three active hits on MolBench. Retrospective evaluation on skill-development tasks shows that evolution increases Qwen's affinity-comparison accuracy from 62.2% to 81.1% and optimization success from 79.5% to 87.2%. In a prospective HPK1 study, DrugHarness achieves a more favorable median docking score than Biomni among system-specific candidates. A synthesized compound achieves a cellular IC50 of 14.19 nM, a 2.64-fold potency improvement over the best input reference, with activity competitive with two selected compounds designed by experienced medicinal chemists. These results support conditional skill evolution for scientific agents and demonstrate a workflow connecting computational drug design with experimental validation.

title: Quantized Mereology
abstract: This paper investigates quantized mereology, which merges quantum information theory with classical mereology, the formal analysis of the part-whole relationship. It emphasizes that information about crisp mereological relations is captured by classical bits, whereas mereological vagueness involves the use of quantum bits, or qubits, to capture mereological information. Transitioning from classical bits to qubits offers a new understanding of part-whole relations among entities that are subject to mereological vagueness. This paper methodically studies the quantized mereology that arises from the classical RCC5 formalism, one of the most widely studied formalisms in Qualitative Reasoning (QR), a subfield of Artificial Intelligence. The argument is made that this method can be extended to quantize more sophisticated QR formalisms, mirroring how strategies are used in physics to transition from classical to quantum systems. The study explores: (i) the conversion of bits to qubits while understanding that these (qu)bits convey mereological information; (ii) the representation of qubit states via set partitions, acknowledging that set theory aligns more closely with classical logic than with the complex vector spaces employed in quantum physics; (iii) demonstrating that classical QR formalisms can be seen as special cases within quantized formalisms; and (iv) showing that qubits more effectively encapsulate information about vague phenomena.

title: Cognitive Surrender and Epistemic Agency in AI-Mediated Education: Code, Results, and Reproducibility Materials
abstract: This repository accompanies “Cognitive Surrender and Epistemic Agency in AI-Mediated Education.” The study combines a conceptual account of cognitive surrender with an exploratory analysis of 16,851 student–LLM interactions from 203 StudyChat users. It examines reliance-oriented interaction patterns, their relationship with visible struggle, contextual variation, and prediction from early interactions. It also proposes a delegation boundary to help educational AI preserve learner judgment and meaningful participation. The package contains analysis code, aggregate results, reproducibility instructions, and sensitivity analyses, including checks that exclude low-context prompting from the Reliance Index. The findings characterize observable behavior without establishing cognitive surrender, diminished learning, or loss of agency. The original StudyChat dataset is not redistributed and must be obtained separately from its source.

title: Volume V: Anatomical Dissection of Quantum Ecosystems: Hardware, Control, Memory and Molecular Pathways against Ecosystem Claims
abstract: This fifth volume performs an anatomical dissection of the claim that quantum leadership will be determined by the construction of a complete ecosystem (hardware, software, networking, sensing, talent and industrialization) rather than by qubit count alone. Each element of the claim is examined against the concrete technical stack developed in the preceding volumes of the series and against established protocols in cryogenic engineering, control electronics, quantum memory and molecular simulation. Modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control are shown to be necessary but not sufficient conditions for the hardware layer; quantum memory specifications and molecular entanglement entropy supply the quantitative criteria that convert raw processor capacity into usable molecular applications; and the dual-clock framing established earlier demonstrates that ecosystem construction is already constrained by migration and architectural lead times that are running independently of any single advantage date. The analysis concludes that ecosystem rhetoric is operationally meaningful only when it is reduced to the measurable interfaces among modular cryogenics, cryogenic control, memory metrics and chemically relevant entanglement.

title: The Collection of a Real-World, Large-Scale Dataset for Automated Skill Evaluation in Central Line Dressing Change
abstract: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs) remain a major source of preventable morbidity and mortality in healthcare settings. Proper execution of the central line dressing change (CLDC) procedure is essential for infection prevention, yet current approaches to competency assessment rely primarily on manual ob- servation by clinical educators, making evaluation time-intensive, difficult to scale, and limited in consistency and granularity. These challenges highlight the need for AI-assisted skill evaluation methods that can support more objective, reproducible, and scalable assessment of clinical performance. However, progress in this area has been constrained by the lack of broad-scale, clinically grounded datasets for developing and evaluating such methods. In this work, we present the collection process of a large-scale video dataset for CLDC skill evaluation, comprising 365 recordings of registered nurses collected during the 2026 annual competency exam at Houston Methodist Hospital. Each video is paired with subtask-level temporal annotations and clinical performance assessments spanning 17 subtasks of the procedure. We describe the data collection and curation pipeline, including pilot testing of record- ing configurations, annotation protocol design, and post-collection processing. We further establish the feasibility of video-based skill assessment through benchmark experiments with spatiotemporal deep learning models. This dataset provides a foundation for future research on automated clinical skill assessment, feedback generation, and AI-assisted training in nursing education.

title: Scaling of entanglement with distance between subsystems: detection of phase transitions in the t'-π-flux model
abstract: The system-size scaling of bipartite entanglement can be used to detect phase transitions. We develop a related approach for strongly correlated electron models where large density matrices or large system size scaling are inaccessible. To this end, we demonstrate that phase transitions of various kinds are signaled by a sharp signature in the first- or second-order logarithmic derivatives of the negativity measuring entanglement between small clusters at varying distances. Crucially, we show how to mitigate the effect of quantum Monte Carlo noise at large distances when computing the negativity. Our focus is on the t'-π-flux Hubbard model using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. It has the particular advantage of showing three distinct phase transitions in a single model: semimetal to band insulator, semimetal to antiferromagnetic Mott insulator, and a magnetic order-disorder transition belonging to the Gaussian, Gross-Neveu, and O(3) Wilson-Fisher universality classes, respectively.

title: E=mc²=i, the entangled pair: dated predictions for the mass of one ebit and for the moment the teleportation heat appears
abstract: Dated predictions, registered before any experiment designed to test them. This is the author's hypothesis. It is not proven, it is not established physics, and it is not a theory of everything. Every prediction lies below the sensitivity of current experiments, so a null result at today's sensitivity neither supports nor refutes it. Building on E=mc²=i (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23415364), where one bit carries the mass of its Landauer energy, kT ln 2 / c², this record applies that formula to an entangled pair. By the author's choice, one maximally entangled pair (one ebit) carries n = 1 bit, held by the relation between the halves, not by either half: 3.2 × 10⁻³⁸ kg at 300 K. Six pair predictions follow (EP1 to EP6: weigh the pair, drop the pair, heat at the detectors, the pair as fuel, locked bits in silicon against the entangled pair, and superdense coding), each set against what standard physics predicts. It also registers P12: the 2 kT ln 2 of heat per teleportation (E=mc²=i P7, cited unchanged) appears at the moment of the Bell-state measurement, even while the outcome record is kept and never erased. A delayed-erasure test is proposed that separates the measurement moment from the record erasure. Open questions are stated as open. Foundation: this record builds on the author's earlier record E=mc²=i (all versions: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23414461), which is itself untested. Its predictions hold only if E=mc²=i holds; a confirmation of E=mc²=i would not by itself confirm the choice n = 1. Falsifier, stated plainly: no excess mass (n = 0) is the result that proves the entangled-pair claim wrong. Prior work: Melvin M. Vopson's mass-energy-information equivalence principle, a stored bit with mass kT ln 2 / c² (Vopson 2019, AIP Advances 9, 095206; test protocol Vopson 2022, AIP Advances 12, 035311), proposed and not yet confirmed. evidence.title: E=mc²=i, the entangled pair: dated predictions for the mass of one ebit and for the moment the teleportation heat appears
evidence.abstract: Dated predictions, registered before any experiment designed to test them. This is the author's hypothesis. It is not proven, it is not established physics, and it is not a theory of everything. Every prediction lies below the sensitivity of current experiments, so a null result at today's sensitivity neither supports nor refutes it. Building on E=mc²=i (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23415364), where one bit carries the mass of its Landauer energy, kT ln 2 / c², this record applies that formula to an entangled pair. A delayed-erasure test is proposed that separates the measurement moment from the record erasure. Open questions are stated as open. title: Exact minimum distances of 27 quantum LDPC codes from recent papers and the qLDPC challenge board (d = 14 to 24)
abstract: This deposit gives exact minimum distances for 27 quantum CSS codes. For each one, the published value was only an upper bound, an interval or an estimate, and as far as we can find the exact value had not been posted. The codes: weight-5 bivariate bicycle codes from J. Cruz-Benito, arXiv:2610.06623: [[432,4]] d = 23, both [[420,4]] classes d = 22, [[420,6]] d = 16, [[432,8]] d = 15, [[420,8]] d = 14; twisted-torus codes from Liang, Liu, Song and Chen, arXiv:2503.03827: d = 22 for [[234,4]], [[246,4]], [[258,4]], [[264,4]], [[280,6]], [[306,8]], [[310,10]], [[312,8]], [[324,8]], [[336,10]], [[342,8]]; covering-graph BB codes from Symons, Rajput and Browne, arXiv:2511.13560: [[140,8]] d = 14, [[192,14]] d = 16, [[192,20]] d = 16, [[224,26]] d = 14; qLDPC challenge board entries: [[454,8]] d = 17, [[316,8]] d = 16, [[280,8]] d = 15, [[210,26]] d = 14, [[510,16]] (board 510-16-24) d = 24; the [[510,16]] generalized bicycle code of Webster, Smith and Cohen (arXiv:2511.15989) and Iceberg Quantum's Pinnacle architecture (arXiv:2602.11457): d = 24. The value 24 is printed there as a conjectured family value; this deposit adds a verification. Method: two separately written exhaustive searches (Python/numba and C), anchored connected-cluster enumeration after Dumer, Kovalev and Pryadko, with symmetry anchoring after Rowshan and Devitt. For 25 codes, each search finds no logical of weight d-1 or less on either side. For the two [[510,16]] codes, both searches exclude weight 22 or less, and since every column has weight 3, every logical has even weight, which rules out 23. Explicit weight-d logicals give the matching upper bound. No machine-checkable certificate is included, so this is a search-based result. The two programs share one method, and LIMITATIONS.md says so. A bug in the second program's quick bound was found during review; it affected codes with column degree above 3. It was fixed, and those codes were rerun. Already-known values are credited, not claimed. G. Lee's bicycle-race database has exact values for codes equivalent to 288-8-20, 266-6-22, 300-8-22 and 210-10-16. Liang et al. give exact values for 248-10-18 and 180-8-16. Our runs agree with these. Contents: code files with check matrices, witnesses, orbits and automorphism generators; both programs; all run logs; one-command quick check (quick_check.sh); hostile review; LIMITATIONS.md. Work done with AI assistants (Claude and ChatGPT) on a home PC.

title: Parametric Resonance in Primal-Dual Learning for Slowly Non-Stationary Constrained MDPs
abstract: Primal-dual methods for constrained Markov decision processes are analyzed under a two-timescale assumption, with non-stationarity entering through two channels. In the additive channel, where the constraint level oscillates, the dual oscillation saturates at a floor set by the moving optimum and is amplified linearly by the timescale ratio. In the parametric channel, where the constraint sensitivity oscillates, a coherent modulation carries no resonant forcing at any depth: the dual update's stiffness modulation cancels the primal update's damping modulation. Instability instead comes from a mismatch between the constraint estimate used by the primal update and the measurement used by the dual update, producing a parametric resonance at twice the pair's natural frequency. The tolerated mismatch grows with the square root of the forcing bandwidth and collapses with the square root of the dual-to-primal step-size ratio. These results hold on the tangent linear-quadratic reduction around an active saddle, for one constraint and for $K$ constraints under a common modulation and an isotropy condition. Driving both updates from the same estimate removes the resonant forcing but introduces a stationary offset equal to the estimator's bias. In a Lagrangian soft actor-critic agent, the multiplier locks onto the sub-harmonic at the timescale ratios its identified linear loop predicts and a coherent cost critic suppresses the lock-in, while a proportional (PID) term, predicted to leave the lock-in in place, suppresses most of it through the projection of the multiplier.

title: Type 1.5 vortex bags in single component Ginzburg-Landau models with higher order potentials
abstract: We demonstrate the existence of type 1.5 like superconductivity in a single component Ginzburg-Landau model with a higher order potential. The model exhibits two competing superconducting Meissner states (MS), each of which has its own pair of length scales (coherence length and penetration depth). The solutions take the form of bags that contain vortices of one vacuum inside the other. This gives rise to four different types of vortex interaction, where one set of length scales determines vortex interactions inside the bags and the other set between the bags. Hence, within the bag the vortices can repel or attract and the bags themselves can repel or attract depending on the hierarchy of four length scales. When vortices repel within the bag, solutions act similarly to those in type 1.5 multicomponent superconductors, but in a single component system.

title: Emergent Behaviour in Financial Markets
abstract: Abstract Some properties of so-called complex or collective systems can be observed to emerge from the interactions of elementary agents. This phenomenon, known as emergent behaviour, has long since been studied in the most diverse disciplines, with recent growing awareness from the formal methods community about the opportunity of opening up to seemingly distant disciplines with appropriate technology for computer-aided reasoning. Different peculiar elements of complexity make automated reasoning on these systems particularly challenging. We consider electronic financial markets to drive our discussion. We identify and structure the sources of complexity to tackle in order to provide computational support for the analysis of emergent phenomena. We refrain from evaluating the suitability of specific technical solutions or frameworks of preference, which would as usual require simplifying assumptions and divert from the actual phenomenon of interest. Rather, we elaborate on possible alternatives to handle some of the main technical aspects involved in automated analysis, while retaining a solid and concrete interpretation of the domain, and in doing so outline a more systematic research program for the formal specification and analysis of market mechanisms.

title: REIMAGINING MARKETING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CASE STUDIES AND MANAGERIAL INSIGHTS
abstract: This document explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in marketing, emphasizing its widespread adoption across businesses of all sizes and the complexities involved in its implementation, such as data privacy concerns and algorithmic bias. The research methodology involves a detailed analysis of real-world case studies from diverse industries, examining how organizations utilize AI-powered tools like machine learning and predictive analytics to enhance customer engagement and optimize marketing strategies. The conclusion highlights AI's potential to create personalized experiences and automate processes, while also stressing the importance of addressing ethical challenges and maintaining consumer trust. It calls for the development of strategies that effectively leverage AI capabilities while prioritizing ethical considerations, and suggests future research directions focused on the long-term impacts of AI on customer loyalty and best practices for integrating AI technologies into existing marketing frameworks.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Technical Project Management: A Critical Incident Study
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports project management tasks in technical, technological and innovation-oriented environments. This paper examines how AI is used in technical project management through a qualitative critical incident technique study. The analysis focuses on a technical subsample of five project managers and 26 selected incidents from information technology, vehicle-related technical projects, technology transfer, innovation management and cybersecurity. The findings show that AI mainly functions as a supportive tool in documentation, information processing, data analysis, idea generation and decision preparation. Its strongest value appears in the planning and execution phases, where it improves efficiency, structure and communication. However, the incidents also reveal risks related to data quality, inaccurate outputs, legal constraints, trust and user acceptance. This study concludes that AI can create value in technical projects only when its use remains combined with human validation, professional judgement and clear responsibility.
