title: Logical rationale and practical paths of digital-intelligence empowerment for improving health education literacy of college physical education teachers
abstract: With the continuous advancement of educational digitalization and health education in colleges and universities, new requirements have been put forward for the professional literacy of college physical education teachers. Based on relevant policy documents and existing studies, this paper analyzes the connotation, improvement logic, realistic adaptation and practical paths of digital-intelligence empowerment for the health education literacy of college physical education teachers. The study holds that this literacy can be understood from four dimensions: health knowledge integration, health information interpretation, health education transformation, and digital-intelligence application and ethics. Its improvement stems from the expansion of health education goals, the integration of physical education and health knowledge, and the collaboration between professional experience and data evidence. At present, there is still room for further improvement in the embedding of health education roles, the connection between physical education and health knowledge, the educational transformation of health data, and relevant support mechanisms. To this end, it is necessary to strengthen the professional role cognition oriented by health promotion, build a knowledge system integrating physical education and health, form a capability chain of "data acquisition – information interpretation – educational decision-making – teaching intervention – feedback adjustment", and improve the support mechanisms of training, teaching and research, interdisciplinary collaboration and evaluation.

title: Darwinian Gating with Goal-Reachable Branch Values: Foundation Alignment and Evidence under Stochastic Availability
abstract: We revise a fail-closed reasoning kernel by separating hard admissibility, goal reachability, counting entropy and stochastic continuation value. The earlier nine-coordinate potential and propagation product remain audited heuristics; neither follows from a physical free-energy law. Inspired by foundational work separating legal sectors, state counts, stochastic transitions and observable projection, we introduce a paper-local acyclic-graph adapter with an explicit goal-completion objective. For independently available edges revealed locally before choice, a sorted continuation backup is proved equivalent to stochastic Bellman optimization. On 600 fixed-seed synthetic graphs, expected completion increases from 57.22% for viability-filtered local ranking and 71.07% for best-path replanning to 73.34%. The paired gain over best-path replanning is 2.28 percentage points (95% interval 2.01–2.55). The new rule matches exact subset Bellman planning, and its advantage over viability disappears when all edges are available. A probability-shift diagnostic and independent Monte Carlo check are included. Earlier public-task and chronological forecasting controls remain parity results. The evidence supports continuation-aware selection under a declared stochastic graph model, not a new universal reasoning law, a CS-derived decision spectrum, or superiority over optimal planners.

title: Neural network optimization-based intelligent evaluation algorithm for international Chinese teaching effect
abstract: Evaluating the effectiveness of teaching Chinese as an international language is considered to be important within the context of global education; as such there is great difficulty in assessing whether or not the way it is delivered is effective due to variances in both learners and their respective learning environments. An intelligent evaluation algorithm based on neural network optimization to address teaching effectiveness problems is developed. The Chaotic Dragonfly Algorithm Optimized Multilayer Feed-Forward Neural Network (CDA-MFFNN) is implemented, to determine a higher level of prediction accuracy for effectiveness in teaching strategies. The data set used to train the CDA-MFFNN model is the Chinese Teaching Effectiveness Data Set, which contains 6,531 data records related to performance, engagement, and instructional attributes. Preprocessing involves min-max normalization and semantic coding of categorical variables, to reduce the number of dimensions and capture latent property patterns. While autoencoders are used as feature extraction method to capture latent patterns and reduce dimensionality. The MFFNN models the relationships between the processed features in a complex non-linear manner while the CDA optimizes the weights of the neural networks to improve convergence and prevent being stuck in local minima during training. Python-based experimental evaluation demonstrated a clear performance advantage over the baseline approaches, with the proposed method attaining 98.65% accuracy and a 98.20% F1-score. It also produced lower prediction errors, recording an MSE of 15.72 and an RMSE of 3.96. This research contributes to the development of intelligent educational analytics and provides action-oriented guidance for curriculum developers and policy makers. Not applicable.

title: Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients
abstract: With infinite-variance gradient noise, SGD can have infinite expected excess objective even when most iterates are close to the optimum. We characterize its accuracy through exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear, constant-stepsize SGD. For regularly varying innovations of index $t\in(1,2)$, the leading measure transports one large gradient shock through the local Hessian flow. This is the same measure that governs the central stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit; we prove its relative accuracy at shrinking tolerances above the central scale, with state-dependent noise and a growing observation horizon. The admissible window is nonempty for every available gradient moment $p>1$. The main technical step is a moment bound at the central fluctuation scale and a lower-moment control of the nonlinear error. The result yields explicit projection and excess-objective tails, extreme quantiles, and a factor $b^{1-t}$ for fixed batch size $b$. For affine population gradients, a sharper comparison gives the same law at fixed tolerances, including random sample Hessians. Coupled simulations in dimensions one to one hundred examine relative calibration, objective quantiles, batch effects, and the error due to random curvature.

evidence.title: Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients
evidence.abstract: With infinite-variance gradient noise, SGD can have infinite expected excess objective even when most iterates are close to the optimum. We characterize its accuracy through exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear, constant-stepsize SGD. For regularly varying innovations of index $t\in(1,2)$, the leading measure transports one large gradient shock through the local Hessian flow. This is the same measure that governs the central stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit; we prove its relative accuracy at shrinking tolerances above the central scale, with state-dependent noise and a growing observation horizon. The admissible window is nonempty for every available gradient moment $p>1$. The main technical step is a moment bound at the central fluctuation scale and a lower-moment control of the nonlinear error. The result yields explicit projection and excess-objective tails, extreme quantiles, and a factor $b^{1-t}$ for fixed batch size $b$. For affine population gradients, a sharper comparison gives the same law at fixed tolerances, including random sample Hessians. Coupled simulations in dimensions one to one hundred examine relative calibration, objective quantiles, batch effects, and the error due to random curvature.

title: Humanity's Last Choice: A Common Evaluation Standard for Generative Engine Optimization
abstract: Humanity's Last Choice describes the idea that the last choice people need to make is which AI system they entrust with the decisions that follow. These systems rely on external sources that content providers can edit through generative engine optimization (GEO) to increase source visibility and influence recommendations. Choosing among these systems therefore requires comparable evidence of how well they carry out user requests when exposed to GEO. Benchmarks have made progress in standardizing tasks, models, and metrics, but they often define their own spaces of GEO strategies and use different editing constraints. These differences can conflate gains from better optimization algorithms with those from greater freedom to edit sources, while making evaluation coverage difficult to compare across benchmarks. We therefore call for a common evaluation standard and propose a meta-taxonomy that describes where sources are edited, how they are edited, and what signals those edits target. Drawing on representative literature, we map existing strategies into a searchable space and outline a protocol for controlled comparisons with explicit coverage reporting. This provides a foundation for common leaderboards that can inform which systems people choose to rely on.

title: The Impact of Retrieval Augmented Generation on the Reliability of Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable fluency but remain fundamentally unreliable for knowledge-intensive tasks due to hallucination, temporal staleness, and lack of verifiability.Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a dominant architectural paradigm that grounds generation in external evidence.This paper provides a comprehensive investigation into how RAG reshapes LLM reliability across factual accuracy, citation fidelity, temporal freshness, and robustness to noise.We benchmark five RAG variants against closed-book baselines using secondary datasets including Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and RGB.Results show an average 23.7% reduction in hallucination rate and 31.2%improvement in citation grounding when using advanced retrieval with self-reflection.However, we identify critical failure modes: retriever-generator misalignment, context distraction, and over-reliance on irrelevant passages.We propose a reliability framework and demonstrate that corrective and modular RAG designs significantly mitigate these risks.Our findings establish RAG as necessary but not sufficient for trustworthy deployment.

title: Drift-Stress v1.0.0: frozen-prompt evaluation harness, per-call logs, and analysis scripts for automatic prompt optimization under data and model shift
abstract: rozen-prompt evaluation harness, frozen prompt artifacts, per-call evaluation logs, and analysis scripts accompanying the article "Does prompt optimization buy robustness? A frozen-prompt evaluation protocol and log-based diagnostics under data and model shift" (B. A. Uluırmak and R. Kurban; submitted to Applied Intelligence). The archive contains: the confirmatory grid: 420 evaluation cells comparing instruction-induction prompt optimization (APE) with an equally grounded unoptimized control on BIG-Bench Hard, GSM8K and arXiv abstract classification, with ten paired seeds, under temporal shift, lexical perturbation, subtask-subset shift and serving-model substitution; the replays under three per-query hard cost caps; the logs of an earlier collapsed-split run, used for the diagnostic analysis in the article. Every number, table and figure in the article can be recomputed from these files without model calls. See README.md for the commands.

title: Geometry vs Binary: Quantum Physics Puzzles — quantum entanglement geometry visualization failur — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: ## Binary Failure → Geometry Solution **Analysis of Findings:** The search results reveal a critical tension: quantum machine learning (QML) researchers are using neural networks to *predict* entanglement patterns, yet the underlying structure of entanglement is fundamentally geometric (e.g., monogamy of entanglement, tensor network geometries). The "exponential separation" result (Zhenhuan Liu, QIP 2025) shows that quantum learning with vs. without purification diverges exponentially — a binary classifier cannot bridge this gap because it lacks a metric for *state purity* that respects the curved manifold of density matrices. **Where binary/statistical approaches FAIL:** 1. **Entanglement classification** — Neural nets trained on entanglement measures (concurrence, negativity) fail to generalize across qubit counts because these measures are not invariant under local unitary transformations. title: AI as a Catalyst for Purpose-Driven Business
abstract: Chapter 7 explores how artificial intelligence is transforming the architecture, culture and governance of modern organisations, revealing both the risks and opportunities of technological acceleration. It argues that AI does not simply automate existing processes but fundamentally reshapes how work is organised, how decisions are made and how value is created. Drawing on the author’s experience redesigning an advisory organisation at Human Planet, the chapter illustrates how AI can invert traditional hierarchical structures, replacing labour-intensive pyramids with lean, purpose-driven systems where experienced professionals are supported by intelligent tools. In this model, technology handles complexity and repetition, while humans focus on judgement, creativity and service. Beyond structural efficiency, the chapter examines the cultural and ethical implications of AI adoption. It highlights how intelligent systems can restore human-centred productivity by removing administrative burdens, enabling organisations to redirect energy towards meaning, collaboration and innovation. At the same time, the chapter warns that AI amplifies the values embedded in an organisation: when guided by vocation and ethical leadership, it strengthens transparency, accountability and stakeholder empowerment; when misaligned, it risks accelerating bias, opacity and institutional failure. Ultimately, Chapter 7 positions artificial intelligence not as a substitute for purpose but as a catalyst that makes organisational vocation more actionable, reinforcing the central premise of the vocating framework: that technology must serve human dignity, long-term stewardship and meaningful contribution.

title: Rethink‐ RAG : Dynamic Retrieval Decision and Cooperative Verification for Reliable Multi‐Hop Question Answering
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable multi‐hop question answering is important for knowledge‐intensive expert systems, where a wrong intermediate fact can propagate into an incorrect final decision. Existing Retrieval‐Augmented Generation (RAG) methods often retrieve for every sub‐question, even when the language model can answer a step from parametric knowledge, and this indiscriminate retrieval can introduce irrelevant or contradictory evidence. We propose Rethink‐RAG, a training‐free framework that combines dynamic retrieval decision with a cooperative answer verification pipeline. The dynamic retrieval decision module generates diverse rewrites of each sub‐question and applies majority voting to decide whether external retrieval is required. The cooperative verification pipeline then filters retrieved documents, quantifies support and opposition through token‐logit evidence, and arbitrates each candidate sub‐answer with an adaptive confidence threshold. Experiments on 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, and MuSiQueQA show that Rethink‐RAG improves answer reliability on knowledge‐intensive reasoning tasks, achieving 49.00% ACC on 2WikiMultihopQA and 49.60% ACC on HotpotQA with the Llama3‐8B evaluator. Additional revision experiments quantify the latency/API‐call trade‐off, sensitivity to the decision‐boundary factor, and the limitations observed on MuSiQueQA, giving a more complete view of the framework's practical operating range.

title: Beyond Multi-Stage Pipelines: A Label-Correlation Ensemble for Multi-Label Retinal Fundus Disease Classification
abstract: Retinal fundus images frequently carry more than one disease, and public fundus datasets are heterogeneous and severely long-tailed. Clinical triage suggests a staged design, in which a screening gate, a disease-group router and group-specific classifiers operate in sequence, but it is unclear whether this hierarchy earns its complexity. We present a controlled comparison of three architectures on a unified 39-target label space built from RFMiD 1.0, RFMiD 2.0 and ODIR-5K (12,652 images): (i) a three-stage gated cascade of eight models, (ii) a flat model with 39 independent sigmoid outputs, and (iii) a label-correlation model that replaces the flat linear head with 39 learned label queries and a two-layer transformer decoder. All three share one Swin-V2-B backbone, one preprocessing pipeline and one training protocol, so differences are attributable to the architecture. Staging offers no consistent advantage: tracing every missed disease instance to the stage that lost it shows that the two coarse gates discard 34.2% of true instances while the fine-grained classifiers lose only 6.7%, and the gates' hard zeros depress the cascade's macro-AUC to 0.747. Label-correlation modeling gives the largest single gain, raising the detection rate from 0.621 to 0.682 (0.689 with test-time augmentation). Blending the flat and label-correlation models under four-view test-time augmentation is the best configuration on six of eight metrics (exact match 0.694, micro-F1 0.678, macro-F1 0.456, macro-AUC 0.972). On definition-matched class subsets it matches or exceeds four recent studies on macro- and micro-F1, most clearly on low-support pathologies. We also show that ensembling a gated cascade with continuous-output models is harmful, and that per-source negative sampling is needed to remove a dataset shortcut that otherwise yields a spurious AUC of 1.000.

title: PanoBench: A Panoptic Occupancy Prediction Benchmark for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Panoptic occupancy unifies 3D geometry, semantics, and instance identities, but its development is limited by scarce instance-aware annotations. Existing benchmarks mainly provide semantic labels reconstructed from incomplete sensor observations, while panoptic datasets have limited domain coverage or annotation completeness. We introduce PanoBench, a camera-centric panoptic occupancy prediction benchmark spanning synthetic and real-world driving scenes. It combines PanoBench-CarlaOcc, PanoBench-nuScenes, and PanoBench-KITTI360 through canonical data interfaces and unified evaluation protocols, providing multi-resolution annotations with persistent instance identities. The synthetic branch derives complete panoptic geometry from simulated meshes. For real-world data, a new pipeline reconstructs backgrounds using geometric priors and topology constraints, generates foreground mesh assets from multi-frame multi-view images, and fuses them into sparse panoptic voxels. A unified valid-mask protocol evaluates complete thing instances supported by temporal observations while scoring stuff regions at the voxel level. Analyses of observation fidelity, geometric completeness, spatial continuity, and temporal consistency demonstrate the benefits of the resulting annotations over existing occupancy benchmarks. We benchmark representative methods on semantic occupancy prediction, panoptic occupancy prediction, and 4D occupancy forecasting, and study voxel resolution, synthetic-to-real transfer, and storage efficiency. These results reveal complementary strengths of volumetric and ray-based metrics and persistent challenges in real-world instance-aware prediction. PanoBench is available at https://mias.group/PanoBench.

title: Temporal Correlations Reshape Causal Resources in Qubit Hamiltonian Recognition: Exact Two-Query Strategy Comparison and a Uniform Critical Crossover
abstract: We investigate binary recognition of an unknown qubit Hamiltonian using two queries of its evolution, with unknown evolution angles that are either independently resampled or shared with tunable temporal correlation. For a symmetric pair of nonorthogonal qubit Hamiltonians, we compare parallel (PAR), sequential (SEQ), and general (GEN) quantum strategies. An exact symmetry reduction expresses the sequential optimization through a three-dimensional correlation elliptope. A general-strategy dual certificate establishes the equality between optimal general and sequential strategies within the studied model. We analyze the operational advantage generated by temporal correlations and establish distinct weak-correlation scaling regimes separated by a critical angle of 45 degrees. This revised and extended version (v1.2) adds a uniform double-scaling critical crossover theorem, including an explicit positive crossover function and consolidated mathematical proofs. The result characterizes a previously unresolved critical transition within the specified quantum Hamiltonian recognition model. The complete mathematical derivations are provided in the accompanying supplementary material (Sections S1–S19). This work is conducted within standard quantum information theory and does not claim physics beyond quantum mechanics. Version: 1.2 Resource type: Publication — Preprint Author: Youfu Wang Affiliation: Independent Researcher, OCN Research
